incident_description:
While using a Bushnell Sportview T1403 432 riflescope mounted on a [REDACTED]-branded .30-06 bolt-action rifle, a safety-related failure occurred. The small metallic turret indicator disc (part of the windage adjustment dial) detached from the scope and fell into the action of the rifle.

The disc became lodged in the bolt and chamber area, jamming the rifles bolt. It was crushed during bolt operation. Although no injury occurred in this case, I believe this incident presents a serious safety hazard due to the nature of how the disc entered the firearms action.

If a shooter were to unknowingly force the bolt closed with the disc obstructing the chamber, it could lead to:

An out-of-battery discharge,
Gas or metal blowback toward the shooter,
Catastrophic failure of the firearm,
and Potential injury or death.
This part failure occurred without abuse or modification. Photos of the damaged scope and the bent disc are available and were submitted to Bushnell Customer Support for review. I am submitting this report to raise awareness and in hopes of initiating a safety evaluation of this failure mode.
justification: The incident involved a safety-related failure of a riflescope, but no injury occurred. The potential for serious injury or death exists if the failure were to occur under different circumstances.

incident_description:
I have used Skoon cat litter for the past few months and every time I open a new bag and pour it, there is a lot (the most of any car litter I've ever seen or used) of dust. Especially for a litter brand that claims 99% dust free. It's a huge dust clouds that lingers and I either walk away for it to settle or push through to get my litterboxes refilled. And then every time I scoop or stir the litter or my cats dig, it kicks up dust again. Well, being made of diatoms, there are silica crystals in the litter. And diatomaceous earth is regulated and not used around animals and limited with humans and not in the home, because it is a powder. But Skoon is unregulated and used specifically for animals and in the home even though it is made of the same thing as DE. Skoon claims safety because it's a pebble and not a powder, but the vast amounts of dust says otherwise. Many people continue to use the product for the pros even though the con of the dust is a problem. 

Yesterday evening, I opened and poured two bags of the  diatom cat litter. Clouds of dust went into the air in my bathroom and while my bathroom fan was on, it was not enough. As it is the middle of winter and the heater is on, I did not open the window this time. I proceeded to refill my litterboxes, all while breathing the dusty air. My chest felt tight after and my breathing became shallow, so I used my rescue inhailer to help. Today, I woke up with heavy/tight lungs that hurt when I breath, and a very spare throat but no swollen tonsils (which would be a sign of sickness, so it doesn't hurt because I'm getting sick, it hurts from inhilation of the dust). I have asthma/use a rescue inhailer sometimes when I get sick with a couch, when I breath extremely cold air, or when the air is heavily polluted. I stay indoors during my areas annual fire season and wear a mask outside if I have to go outside. I am just lying in bed currently and my lungs feel like I've just run a mile. I'm hoping with some use of my inhailer, the effect goes away and I won't have to go to the doctors. Today I realized my cats have been coughing/hacking/throwing up more frequently in the last few months, since I've started using Skoon cat litter. If it's dusty every time I pour new litter out, and every time I scoop and stir the cat litter, then it's dusty every time they dig/use it too. Which means their lungs are also being affected. Since they clean themselves by licking, any dust that settles on their fur or paws is also being inhaled/ingested. 

I am stopping use of this litter and switching back to grass seed litter which has much lower amounts and non diatom dust. I will continue to monitor my breathing, use my inhailer, and seek a doctor if it does not improve in a few days or gets worse.
justification: The user and their cats experienced respiratory issues, including tight chests, shallow breathing, and coughing, after exposure to the dusty cat litter. The symptoms indicate an injury or adverse health effect, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the repeated exposure to the dusty litter.

incident_description:
I am submitting this report to raise awareness and seek immediate investigation into the Tidy Cats Breeze Cat Litter Pellets, manufactured and sold by Purina, due to severe and life-threatening health risks posed by this product. The product, containing Modernite Zeolite as the main ingredient, has been linked to numerous cases of serious illnesses and death in cats, as well as potential health risks to humans. 

 Summary of Health Concerns: 
 1. Harm to Cats:
  Several verified reviews on Amazon and other platforms have documented cases of cats ingesting these litter pellets, leading to critical health issues including severe non-regenerative anemia, kidney failure, heart failure, and death. 
  In my personal experience, one of my cats ingested the Tidy Cats Breeze pellets and subsequently became gravely ill. X-rays revealed that his abdomen was filled with the pellets, which do not dissolve in water, making them impossible to pass naturally. 
  Cats that ingest these pellets or lick their paws after using the litter are at risk of ingesting toxic substances released by the product. These substances have been linked to catastrophic health outcomes. 

 2. Documented Cases and Evidence: 
  Online reviews, social media groups, and direct outreach from other consumers highlight that my case is not isolated. Numerous cat owners have reported similar outcomes, with many cats succumbing to illness despite medical intervention. 
  Published articles have drawn connections between zeolite, the primary component of these pellets, and various health issues in animals, including cancer, anemia, and organ failure. 

 3. Risks to Humans: 
 The dust generated by this litter poses serious health risks to humans, particularly pregnant women, children, and babies, who may inhale or come into contact with the dust. 
  Given the widespread use of this product in households, the potential human exposure to the harmful effects of zeolite through inhalation or ingestion is concerning. 

 Purinas Response: 
  When I contacted Purina regarding my cats illness caused by the ingestion of these pellets, they offered to cover my veterinary bills, but only under the condition that I sign a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA). I refused to sign the NDA, as it became evident that Purina is aware of the risks posed by this product and has attempted to suppress information regarding the harm it causes. 
  Despite numerous complaints from consumers, Purina continues to sell the product, seemingly prioritizing profit over the well-being of pets and consumers. 

 Financial and Emotional Impact: 
  I have personally incurred thousands of dollars in veterinary bills trying to save my cat in 2022. Many other pet owners have reported similar financial burdens, while some have lost their pets altogether. 
  The emotional toll on families who have lost their beloved pets to this dangerous product is immeasurable.

 Call to Action: 
  I urge the Consumer Product Safety Commission to investigate Purinas Tidy Cats Breeze Cat Litter Pellets and consider enforcing a recall due to the products toxicity. 
  It is imperative that proper labeling and warnings are provided regarding the severe health risks associated with the use of this litter. 
  Furthermore, the Commission should look into potential violations of consumer safety regulations, especially considering Purinas knowledge of the harm and their attempts to silence affected consumers with NDAs. This product continues to pose a serious threat to both cats and humans, and immediate action is necessary to prevent further harm.
justification: The incident description reports multiple cases of death in cats and potential health risks to humans, indicating a high severity level. The frequency of reported cases and the manufacturer's alleged awareness of the risks suggest a likelihood that is likely rather than rare or unlikely.

incident_description:
We used InkBird thermostats to control our reptile enclosures.  Over the past few months we have had three of their devices fail.  The failure was the exact same on all devices.  Details:
- Devices were set to maintain a temperature of 88 degrees Fahrenheit
- The devices lost control and caused the heat pads to reach 102, 115, and 140 (where we caught the separate temperatures for the three failed devices).
- The device probe was accurately reading the high temperatures but wasn't doing anything to control it.

We were home for the first two failures and caught them in time but we were out for the evening for the third failure.  It reached temperatures high enough to melt plastic in the enclosures and unfortunately killed 5 of our geckos.

All three devices failed shortly after their two year date of purchase.  We were not even close to using the total wattage that the devices are rated for.  We were in fact only using less than a third of their rated capacity.  All were on separate circuits in the house.

I emailed InkBird to notify them and their solution was to attempt sending me  a new device and couldn't have cared less.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of 5 geckos due to overheating caused by device failure. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as only three devices failed out of presumably many devices used over an extended period.

incident_description:
I purchased Ceramic Paint from "A Makers' Studio" (https://amakersstudio.com/collections/ceramic-paint/products/ceramic-paint-bundle). Their website claims it is food safe. However, when I received my order, I saw that the paint bottle said it is washable between 56 to 104 degrees. That sounded odd since my dishwater even when I hand wash is up to 120 degrees. I called the company to ask about this, and they said while I'd probably be okay handwashing it at 110-115, it starts to disintegrate and come off at 150 degrees and it should not be heated above that. Since food and drinks are hotter than 150 degrees in many cases - coffee, tea, food out of oven or off the stove, it is clearly not food safe as advertised and should not be used on mugs, plates or bowls. It also has a very strong odor that reminds me of how wall paint from Home Depot smells. I asked for a Safety Data Sheet, but have not received one.

I have since followed up with company and asked for a full refund but have not heard back.
justification: The incident involved a product mislabeled as food safe, potentially leading to consumer exposure to unsafe materials, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of occurrence appears possible given the product's intended use and the company's misleading advertising.

incident_description:
I experienced long-term chemical exposure from an unused chemistry lab kit made by Science Interactive. It was stored in its original box in a shared bedroom up on a shelf in the closet. Without my knowledge, the liquid chemicals were evaporating and forming gases, causing me respiratory issues for months starting around February 2023. I had it for a year and a half when the respiratory issues started because of the kit. I experienced coughing if I had been near where the kit was stored, such as sitting at my desk, and I would also get a burning sensation in my lungs. During these months the burning feeling would last around half an hour after leaving the area and would become a lighter irritation after more time passed. I noticed that the symptoms would only start when I was in my room around that area. Not knowing the cause, I got an air purifier for the desk, which didn't help. I also searched for mold, and I contacted a testing company. I suspected a chemical was causing the symptoms, but I didn't suspect the kit at that point because nothing inside had been opened. I was concerned and tried to avoid the area while also trying to figure out the cause. I then started to clean out the room. In May I emailed Science Interactive asking how to dispose of the unused lab kit.

On May 31st I opened the box and saw that the chemicals had been evaporating because there was little liquid in the bottles. I was scared but quickly took a few pictures to show a professor and then closed the box. Minutes later I started coughing and experiencing the familiar burning sensation, so I then knew this was what had been causing my respiratory issues. I messaged a professor and brought the kit to campus with the help of her instructions. Even after removing it, I continued to experience the burning sensation for many days. I emailed Science Interactive explaining the situation and asked to speak with someone about their product's safety or a chemistry expert. There were so many liquid chemicals in the kit that I was concerned not knowing what harmful chemicals could be formed with them evaporating and reacting with each other. The representative ignored my request and just said to dispose of the kit "to prevent further discomfort.ÃÂ This situation has been extremely upsetting. Science Interactive must disclose the possible gases that could be formed from the storage of the chemicals in their kit so that I know what health effects could result and can inform healthcare professionals.

Because there were no instructions for storage of the kit, I had asked the professor when I dropped the class if the unused kit could be kept longer. I originally intended to retake the class, and he told me it should be fine to still have it for if I was going to retake the class at a later semester. When I also asked again about it this year the professor said that similar bottles of chemicals were stored in the school lab for many semesters without problems and that the chemicals don't ordinarily age. I don't know if he could have anticipated that the chemicals werenÃÂt sealed well, but I wouldn't have brought it into my home around me and my family if I had known. It was kept around room temperature, but it wasn't a strictly controlled environment, and there were no warnings that it needed to be. I'm very worried about what health effects this could have. After opening the kit and experiencing the burning sensation for days, I since have started having reoccurring acid reflux, something I didnÃÂt have before, along with increased lung sensitivity. I also have a hard swollen lymph node for months that I didnÃÂt have before. Representatives from both Science Interactive and the college didnÃÂt address my concerns, ignoring many of my questions or giving vague responses. This was difficult to write about because itÃÂs such a shocking situation that has left me very shaken. I submitted a report in August when I found this site, but I asked to be able to rewrite it because I didnÃÂt submit it properly.

UPDATED ON 8/12/2024: [To update, this whole event has caused a lot of trauma and the lack of any kind of explanation or help has left me despondent. I have blamed myself for not taking more pictures of the contents of the box even though the kit was actively causing my lungs to burn, so my instinct was not to get closer and look at it more but to keep it away from myself and others. 
- The comment made by Science Interactive is false. I did have chemical exposure from the kit, and removing the kit stopped the burning lungs sensation and coughing. I was able to sit at the desk in the room again with no symptoms whatsoever after removing the kit. My symptoms improving after removing the kit from the area is detailed in medical records and also emails and texts with professors. I can provide these records. 
- TO BE CLEAR, I did NOT see every item in the kit as I very hastily took a picture of the material list, one of the bags of chemicals, and closed the lid again and then began to experience the burning and coughing minutes later. The mention by the manufacturer of "staining" in the box that I did not report is not something I can say was or wasn't there as I did not see everything in the box. Many items were covering each other, and I opened and closed the box as fast as I could. If something other than only just the chemicals themselves was involved, for example, the fuel burner or other item in the box, I completely admit I did not look at other items, as I was terrified and breathing the gas inside proved harmful because my lungs soon started burning after opening the box. I was in a state of panic. My instinct was not to go back to the box and look at everything when it was making my lungs burn. The fact that I did not look at each item is not proof that this did not happen. It did happen. I WISH it didn't. I thought at the time that the college or professors would do an investigation of the kit. In the moment, I was scared and trusting the professor to tell me exactly what to do and initially she said to throw the kit in the garbage, which didn't sound safe to me to put something actively giving off an unknown gas into the garbage that another person might pass by, so I asked if I could bring it to the college. She said to put it in a bag, so I did. She wasn't present at the campus, but I did as instructed and took it where she told me to.
- I have notified a total of two Chemistry professors about the long-term chemical exposure I experienced. Neither professor provided an explanation about what thing or things in the kit could have been the cause, even though I asked repeatedly. I also asked if the kit was investigated after I dropped it off at the school. This question was also ignored.
- I emailed the school board about what happened because the professors didn't provide me with any explanation. I thought the school would investigate, but the board did not respond to me at all. I said I didn't want to be ignored, and they ignored me. 
- The Consumer Product Safety Commission also has not contacted me further.   
- I took measurements of where the kit was on the shelf, how high off the ground, and measurements in relation to the desk I would sit at when I would start coughing, lungs burning. The kit was stored nearly 7 feet off the ground, and the gas was still reaching me despite that height. I have photos of the measurements and the room this was happening in. 
Measurements: 
* The box was stored on the highest shelf in the closet, 6 feet and 11 inches off the ground. 
* The chair I would sit at was around 5 feet and 6 inches over from where the box was stored.
* The height of the chair was around 3 feet and five inches from the ground. My head would be about a foot above this. 

I mentioned I found swollen lymph nodes following this prolonged exposure. One of them in particular is the most noticeable to me because it hurts daily from just everyday movements. The company's side comments about how long the kit was kept being "unusual" has no relevance to my report as there were NO instructions about the length of time it was safe to store. NONE. Not with the kit, not on their website. No student should experience chemical exposure due to your lack of proper instructions. I had dropped the class. Students drop classes all the time. incident_description:
On February 20, 2023, I purchased this product (order # [REDACTED]):
WIEZ GPS Wireless Dog Fence, Electric Dog Fence,Pet Containment System,Range 65-3281ft, Adjustable Warning Strength, Rechargeable, Harmless and Suitable for All Dogs(New Model for 2023!)  

That product was purchased from the Amazon website and charged to my Amazon credit card, billed as an Amazon purchase.

The product says in its title its safe for dogs. The reviews were very positive. I relied on that information to make, what I thought to be, an informed decision.

However, the dog collar malfunctioned and shocked my dog with electricity for several minutes straight. The dog was only a few feet from the center of the area he should have been able to use. He should have been able to walk more than 60 feet away with no shock.

Additionally, when I was finally able to get the collar off of him, it shocked me so badly I yelled out loud and dropped it. This shock occurred despite the fact that the product was set on the lowest level available for the shock. I am 160 pounds. This product was marketed as appropriate for my 16 pound dog. 

The collar took minutes to remove because the dog was flailing and it is snugly fit against his throat. It appeared to be giving the highest level of shock although it was clearly set at the lowest level.

My dog will not allow me to put anything like this around his neck now and will not go out back with me anymore, despite the fact that he would never be more than 2 feet from me regardless of whether I am inside or outside, prior to this event. 

I have people that will testify as witnesses on my behalf. 

Amazon is very clear on its website that it does not tolerate vendors attempting to alter reviews or paying people to alter or delete their review. The verbiage chosen by Amazon to describe the intolerance of these acts is extremely clear.

However, when wrote a very honest review of the product and its horrific malfunction, the vendor did in fact offer me money to take my review down. I reported that event to Amazon and described the product malfunction and the extreme pain it caused my dog. Instead of intolerance, I found the vendor had apparently never been contacted by Amazon about paying me to take down my review. In fact, the vendor continued to offer me $125 to take the review down. A very motivating amount of money for many people.

So now I relied on reviews to be accurate, because of AmazonÃÂs extremely clear policy of intolerance for alteration or deletion of bad reviews. But that intolerance is actually nonexistent in my case, which leads me to believe other people have likely written reviews about this product malfunctioning. Those reviews would have steered me away from this product. In fact, after looking at many products similar to this one, I chose this one because the reviews gave no hint of safety problems. But those reviews can be falsified.

My dog was in extraordinary pain while he was being shocked. He now cannot even go out in back anymore. I cannot use any type of dog fence collar on him anymore. He thinks something is in the back that attacked him and lives in fear of it.

My dog and I may be luckier than some. If I left home to go to the store he could have been shocked for an hour or more straight. IÃÂd guess a dog would likely die of a heart attack from that. Maybe from self injury due to flailing every which way to try to get away from the very powerful shock. 

Amazon misled me in an extraordinary way by leading me to believe reviews are generally unaltered, when in actuality I have evidence that Amazon takes no action to stop review tampering, even when its reported directly to them.

This also makes me realize that Amazon sells many products that can be safety hazards. Some are even identified as medical devices. All of those may have skewed sets of reviews, due to review tampering. This makes me feel that the CPSC, FDA and other groups need to put out advisories.
justification: The dog was injured and in extraordinary pain from being shocked by the malfunctioning collar, and the owner was also shocked and injured.

After about 5 minutes, some of the basement lights shut off unexpectedly, and our daughter said the cat toy broke.  I checked our home electrical panel and noticed the breaker tripped on one of the basement circuits.  Wondering what could have overloaded the circuit, I noticed the cover of one of the wall outlets was blackened as if from a small electrical fire.  We realized when our daughter was swinging the aforementioned cat toy around with its metal wire, it accidentally got wedged between the wall outlet and the plug of the electronic dartboard in our basement.  This caused a short circuit, a small electrical explosion at the wall outlet, and literally burned the wire of the cat toy in two.  Luckily our circuit breaker functioned as it should and cut power with no injury to our daughter.

We feel this cat toy should come with a warning that there is a shock hazard because of the metal wire, or at least a warning that it cannot be used by children without adult supervision.  We realize this was a freak occurrence and not every hazard needs a warning.  But it is not something that crossed our mind as parents, so we felt obligated to report this.
justification: The incident involved a short circuit and small electrical explosion but resulted in no injury. The likelihood of such an occurrence is unlikely as it required a specific sequence of events.

I would benefit greatly from a more detailed list of products that do or would be likely to contain this chemical so that I can try to resume a somewhat normal life like I had prior to the exposure. incident_description:
I bought a K&H Pet Products 20 inch heated pet bed for our 14 year old black cat with arthritis. It arrived on December 28th & our cat developed a deep bond with the bed. He only ever left it to use the litter box, eat & drink. Otherwise he was in pure cushy bliss. I had the pet heating pad correctly inserted under the 6 inch cushion of the bed, plugged in & the cord gently tucked between our living room leather couch's cushion and armrest so it wouldn't get tangled, twisted, or possibly clawed by our cat. The information I've seen about the bed was that the heating pad was specifically designed for pets, & was pressure activated. Purportedly the heating pad would maintain a lower temperature when not in use.
On Friday 1st January, we entered the living room to find our cat cowering under our Christmas tree, which was extremely unusual for him. There was a puddle of vomit next to him, & he was quite noticeably shaking. When I tried to approach him to see what was wrong, he hissed at me. I checked the pet bed & found it was soaking wet with urine, as was the couch underneath... all the way down to the flooring. 
At first I thought he must be dealing with a urinary tract infection, as he's had those in the past. I unplugged the heating pad, separated it from the bed & washed the entire pet bed thoroughly. It wasn't until Saturday night that I changed my mind, as our cat, [REDACTED], still wasn't acting  right. He wasn't eating or drinking, or really moving for that matter. His hind legs barely worked. He had no strength to jump up onto furniture at all. He scuttled around as if he was trying to escape something that terrified him. He didn't use his litter box, nor did he go anywhere else.
On Sunday night, the 3rd, I found the burns. [REDACTED] wanted to jump up onto an old computer chair, but couldn't, so I carefully scooped him up. He hissed AND tried to bite me. He NEVER does that unless he's in a lot of pain. My one hand came away a little wet from where it'd been just behind his front legs.
On Monday the 4th, I called our vet first thing & she had me drop [REDACTED] off for an examination. She found three distinct burns on his belly between his front and rear legs. They were severe. She had to gas him unconscious so she could clean & debride the burns. She gave him IV fluids & a strong antibiotic shot.
Our vet isn't sure how the burns were exactly caused, but I can't find any breaks in the electrical cord or heating pad that would indicate he'd chewed or clawed into it. She did check, & he does not have a urinary tract or bladder infection. But the burns were definitely from the heating pad.

incident_description: While changing my whole-home water filter I leaned my arm on my Olympic Kiln and got shocked (240V-1 phase). I investigated, first checking my home wiring then checked the kiln. I found that there was an open limit to ground. Although the kiln is still under warranty, I opened the plug (a large 240V plug) and found that the ground wire was not attached. The kiln is wired using liquid tight conduit as a power cord. From my research, I don't think that is up to code. It also has a four prong plug but only three of the prongs are connected. I also discovered that the kiln bears a UL Listed label but the product doesn't appear in the UL directory (these items were reported to UL). I contacted the Olympic Kilns. They want me to reattach the ground wire on the plug. They would not address the other concerns I had about the conduit and the plug. I am concerned that someone could get killed. I am lucky that I leaned on the kiln and the electricity pushed me away. If I had grabbed the kiln, I may have been drawn to it. I think that Olympic Kilns may be manufacturing products that are not up to NEC (National Electric Code). What I found in the NEC section 422.43 (b) sounds like conduit is not allowed as a power cord. I wasn't able to find out if using only three prongs of a four prong plug is code compliant. I don't know where to go to make them produce safe consumer products.
justification: The incident involved a 240V electrical shock, but no injury occurred. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible due to the identified electrical safety issues with the kiln's wiring and plug.

During the walk, the dog ÃÂtook off at a dead runÃÂ and a split second later the user heard a ÃÂpopÃÂ and then felt something strike him in his left eye. A mechanical buckle on the leash unintentionally separated resulting in the leash quickly retracting and striking him in his left eye, causing serious injuries.  The plastic buckle itself was not damaged by this separation and continued to appear to function normally.  The user had been given this retractable leash as a gift (in new, unused condition) from a neighbor approximately two weeks before his accident and he used it on a daily basis from that time up until the time of his accident.  He also indicated that the buckle that came apart at the time of his accident had also done so before, on the very first occasion he used it to walk his dog.  In that previous situation, the detached leash came whipping back at him causing the buckle to strike him in his hand but without further incident. 

The leash incorporates a means of attaching the leash body to the userÃÂs waist (i.e. attachment to oneÃÂs belt) and also a separable non-retractable portion of the leash that can be quickly connected or disconnected from the retractable portion by means of a plastic coupling. The leash design also includes a typical handle containing the spool around which the leash wraps and a constant force spring winding mechanism that retracts the leash (similar to the arrangement of a typical retractable tape measure).  The leash itself is a 14ÃÂ long rope leash attached by a two-part plastic side release buckle to a 3ÃÂ long section of nylon webbing which is then attached to the dogÃÂs collar with a metal clip.  

Research

The hazards of retractable dog leashes were known prior to the invention of the subject dog leash.  There are many CPSC NEISS case narratives of retractable dog leash accidents spanning the years 2002 ÃÂ 2009 that involve a leash breaking, retracting and striking the user in the face or some other body part.  

The safety booklet included with the M2 Hip Hugger leash acknowledges this hazard.  The booklet includes statements such as:
ÃÂ	ÃÂIf the leash separates from the collar and safety loop during use, immediately apply brake and turn your face away.ÃÂ
ÃÂ	ÃÂIf not fully retracted, the leash cord/belt can retract rapidly and the hook can cause eye and face injury.ÃÂ  
ÃÂ	ÃÂIf your dogÃÂs collar breaks, the safety loop will stay attached to your dog.  This will prevent the cord/belt from retracting rapidly and the hook from possibly hitting you causing eye or face injury.ÃÂ

Testing

Leash Retraction Speed
We filmed the retraction of the leash to determine its velocity. The maximum leash retraction speed is approximately 35 mph and the entire retraction event occurs in approximately ÃÂ½ second, which is too short of an interval to expect a user to react to an unexpected stimulus and take evasive action, such as pressing the leash brake on the handle or turning away from the leash as suggested in the instruction booklet.

Dog Testing
In order to evaluate the tensile loads that could be placed on the leash while walking a dog, we tested the leash pull-force that was generated by a surrogate dog (a 41 lb Brittany) on a standard, non-retractable 5ÃÂ long leash.  During this testing, the surrogate dog generated peak leash loads in the range of 70-92 lbs (i.e. up to 2.2 times its own weight).  Therefore, a leash that is sold for use with a 100 lb dog should be able to withstand tensile forces of over 220 lbs.  

Plastic Buckle Strength
We performed quasi-static tension strength tests on a group of exemplar M2 Hip Hugger retractable leashes.  Some of the buckles were tested in a new, completely unused condition, while others underwent pre-test buckling and unbuckling to simulate the condition of a slightly used buckle.  During each test, the plastic buckle was loaded in tension with a static weight.  During the testing of one of the new exemplar Hip Hugger leashes, the plastic buckle separated when loaded with 95.5 lbs.  Prior to separating, while under load, the male part can be seen pulling out of the female part of the plastic buckle.  The separated plastic buckle did not break and did not show any signs of structural failure.  Another exemplar Hip Hugger leash we tested (this one was purchased used) failed in a similar manner multiple times without any visible damage.  That side release buckle came apart at a tensile force of approximately 30 lbs.
justification: The incident resulted in a serious injury to the user, who was struck in the left eye by the retracting leash, and the design defect was found to cause the leash to fail at a tensile force as low as 30 lbs, indicating a high likelihood of similar incidents occurring.

incident_description: My 8 month old baby was playing with a soft book ("A is for Animals" by Kids Preferred). The book has a "bookmark", which is a string with one end attached to the top of the plastic book binding, while the other end has two plastic shapes (one circle, one star) that the baby likes to chew on. My baby was lying on the floor on her back while playing with the book. Suddenly, she ended up with the book stuck under one side of her head and the plastic shapes stuck under her head on the other side, with the string "bookmark" strangling her across her neck. She started turning red in seconds. She screamed and I was able to remove the book before any damage was done, but it became clear to me that the string "bookmark" is a serious strangulation hazard.
justification: The incident involved a near-strangulation with immediate physical distress (turning red, screaming), but no lasting injury occurred. The likelihood of this specific event is considered possible given the design of the bookmark and common baby play behaviors.

incident_description:
I have a Yamaha electronic keyboard model PSR225GM. When I attempted to unplug the power supply from the outlet the box it was housed in came apart in my hand. This is very similar to a recall Yamaha had on a similar power unit for a different model of keyboard. 
If I had been less careful when the box came apart, if I were a child for example, I would have grabbed the unit that remained plugged into the outlet and received a life threatening electrical shock. 

The wall adapter I got with the keyboard was marked "Lo Duca" as the manufacturer. It appears identical to the earlier recall even though it doesn't carry the Yamaha brand on it.
justification: The incident involved a potential risk of electrical shock but did not result in injury. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given the similarity to a previous recall.

incident_description:
(04/27/2014) The consumer stated her child was on the floor playing with the book. He had the book for about three minutes and was able to take the three of the little plastic eyes from one of the characters.

There are about ten plastic eyes throughout the book. The child had two of the eyes  in his hands and was putting one in his mouth.

The consumer stated that the book indicates that it meets ASTM F963 and CPSC safety requirements.
justification: The incident involved a child removing small parts from a book, which were then handled in a way that posed a choking hazard, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of such an incident is unlikely given that the book met certain safety standards.

incident_description:
In December I purchased the Kids Made Modern Stamp Set at Target. Today my kids and I went to use the stamp pads for a project and found what appears to be mold growing on them. I have attached 3 pictures of the pads with the growth on them so you can see what I mean.

I would suggest that this product be recalled and all stamp pads made by this brand re-evaluated. Luckily I was with my children so I could keep them from touching the pads, but other kids might get closer or want to touch them to see what it is.
justification: The incident involved mold growth on stamp pads, posing a potential health risk, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it was a singular incident with a specific product.

incident_description: At approximately 1 am on March 28th, 2014, my wife and I were awakened to the smell of smoke in our house.  We discovered that our automatic litter box, sold under the name "Cat Genie" by a company by the name of PetNovations, was on fire.  We immediately unplugged the unit, and once the fire was out, removed it from our home.  I received a minor burn to my right palm while attempting to remove the unit from our home.  I did not require medical attention for the burn.  I later disassembled the main power unit and took pictures of the inside, which I will attempt to attach to this report.  I contacted the manufacturer's customer service via email the next day.  Today I received a call from a supervisor in their customer support center and was told this was a common problem and that the unit was designed with specific safeguards to prevent fires.  He also stated that by looking at the pictures of the charred insides of the unit, the safeguards "worked as designed".  I was stunned by that statement.  He stated that they would send us a check for the cost of the unit (we purchased it in May of 2012 and it was still under warranty), and would also be willing to pay a company to clean the smoke smell from our home.  He then emailed me a shipping label and asked that I ship the power unit back to the company so their engineers could examine it.  I have not shipped the unit back yet, and am hesitant to do so pending further investigation by an independent source.  Had this happened in the middle of the day when my wife and I were both gone, I am certain our house would have burned to the ground.
justification: The severity level is 3 because the incident resulted in a minor injury (a burn that did not require medical attention). The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) because although the incident did occur, the manufacturer's response suggests that the product has safeguards to prevent fires, and there is no indication that such incidents are common.

incident_description: NAFD Engine 2 was dispatched to the address for a mattress fire that was already out, but the home owner wanted us to make sure. A  child had taken some hampster bedding out of a pet toy and while playing with it on her bed near a lit candle on her nightstand. The bedding came into close proximity of the candle and it ignited. It was dropped on the bed where it caught the bed spread and mattress on fire. No injuries reported.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was already extinguished by the time responders arrived, and no injuries were reported. The fire was caused by a child's actions with a candle and flammable material, making it a preventable incident with some likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: I want to report a laceration safety hazard with a child's product called "Art 101ÃÂ®, Tri-fold Art Set" manufactured in China by "DM Creations Int'l Ltd.", located at "18/F, Two ChinaChem Plaza, Hong Kong". They post a US phone number (877) 927-8101, and email: customerservice@art101usa.com. The vinyl covered box-like package contains drawing and coloring utensils (made in Vietnam). I wish to report that the "seams and edges" of the container that have been heat welded are razor-sharp! I just went to move some items that surrounding this play set in my child's room and inadvertently brushed my hand in an upward motion along the seam. I sustained a very deep cut on my left index finger that should be stitched. I can't imagine what this might do to my 5 or 4 year old children. The manufacturing process could have included an last step of melting the edges into a round or bull nosed finish. I recommend that this product be examined and recalled if necessary due to it's hazardous packaging.
justification: The incident resulted in a deep cut that required stitches, indicating a moderate to severe injury. The sharp seams and edges are a design flaw that could potentially harm multiple users.

incident_description: I had a severe allergic reaction after being exposed to this item for just a few minutes.  This was after being assured by a customer support representative that the products did NOT contain latex.  Obviously they do, or else I would not have had an allergic reaction.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury due to a severe allergic reaction, and it was caused by misinformation from customer support. The likelihood of this occurrence is unlikely as it involved a specific product and incorrect information.

incident_description: This is a children's book, I love you honey bunny by [REDACTED]. It has bendable fabric bunny ears that stick out of the top of the book. I've had this book about 10 months, and as my child was recently playing with it and bending its ears a stiff metal wire poked out of the fabric. Probably about 3 inches in length and scratched my daughter on the leg. It was not a serious injury at all but I am concerned with how stiff the metal wire is that it could poke and injure a child's eye.
justification: The incident resulted in a minor injury, as the metal wire scratched the child's leg. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it was a one-time event with a specific product.

incident_description: My child received a RoseArt Extreme 3D 3-in-1 Spin Art for Christmas, my daughter decided to use it for the first time today. I put the batteries in it, loaded the paper, and turned on the lights and motor. She opened the first bottle of ink and used it properly, squeezing the bottle just enough to let a few drops out. She closed the lid and moved to the next bottle. She opened it, turned it upside down and squeezed. When she did this, just as she had previously done, the top of the bottle flew off causing the entire bottle to empty onto the spinning paper. The ink was splattered not only on my 4 year old daughter, but on myself, and my 18 month old who was nearby. It was splattered into my youngest daughters eyes and all over her face and neck. I had to immediately wash her eyes out, causing her to scream and cry. Im not sure if it was painful or not, having the ink in her eyes because she is too young to tell me. I put both children in the bath tub to wash them down as this was supposed to be "washable" ink. However, both of their faces, necks, and hands are stained with blue ink. I called the RoseArt company and they do not want to help me in any way with reporting this incident. All the woman was concerned with over the phone was explaining to me that they do not offer monetary reimbursement or that they could send a replacement product. My concern was not with money or a new toy for my daughter, it was to inform them that their product was unsafe. They did not care.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to a 4-year-old child, with ink getting into her eyes, face, and neck, and required immediate washing out of her eyes. The product's design allowed for uncontrolled ink release, posing a risk of similar incidents.

incident_description: I purchased Grafix Glow Swirling Art Set for my daughters for Christmas of 2013 and they opened this today to play with and as I tried to squeeze the paint out it shot directly into my eyes causing very painful burning, I then proceeded to wash the paint out. Later this evening I am still experiencing pain and itching and a headache. I've seen reports of this product before for the same reason.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, as the paint caused painful burning, itching, and a headache. The likelihood of occurrence is likely due to previous reports of similar incidents with the same product.

incident_description: my son began playing with a new Grafix "Glow Swirling Art Set" when the first bottle of 'swirl paint' was opened it exploded and the paint and cap shot into his eye causing immense pain and subsequent eye injury.  When an adult near him tried to understand the cause of the accident the second bottle to be opened also exploded with dramatic force, thankfully not in their face.  This product has a history on the internet of the same injury from over 4 years ago and should be seriously investigated.
justification: The incident resulted in an eye injury, and there is a documented history of similar incidents, indicating a possible pattern of product malfunction.

incident_description:
There are items on e-bay geared towards pet owners.  While it might seem fun to a consumer it is dangerous to the pet.  These laser pointers one in particular FroliCat Bolt Automatic Laser Light Teaser Toy has an adjustable mirror which can allow a consumer to tilt the laser to the point of getting the laser into the pet's eyes.  These lasers are dangerous to sight.  They can blind an animal or human if these lasers are directed directly towards an eye.  These can be used unattended.  While the cat may chase the point of light many kittens and older cats will look to see where the light is coming from.  I know my cats are smart and especially the one of mine who jumps on our printer to try to see how the paper travels in the front and comes out the front.  She always tries to figure out how it turns the paper around.

These should be removed from the market before someone or someone's pet gets really hurt.
justification: The incident can cause injury to pets, potentially leading to blindness, and the product can be used unattended, increasing the risk. The description does not indicate a specific incident has occurred, but the potential for injury exists.

incident_description:
The caller stated that the design of the dye when opened causes laceration.  The dyes are used for card making through a press.  She received a minor punctured wound on her finger because she was trying to pull it apart to use it.   No medical attention was received.  She stated that there are other distributors who make these dyes with the steel component.

(3/2013) The manufacturer was contacted through email but she did not receive a response.  She feels that this product is a safety hazard and should be investigated.

The consumer has further investigated this matter, and the following is an update:

1.  The consumer contacted another distributor, other than Memory Box, who stated that all the smaller
companies such as hers; Memory Box; Poppystamps; [REDACTED]; [REDACTED],
and others, have their stamps made by the same steel die manufacturer in the USA. She
refrained from giving me the name of the manufacturer.
2. The consumer have enclosed some photographs of steel dies from Poppystamps (a subsidiary of
Memory Box). You will note the dies are produced as one piece, held together by little
steel bits. In order to separate the pieces, one must bend them back and forth, gently, to
break them, or, they must use scissors or wire snips. It is the little steel bits that remain
that are the culprits. It is very easy to puncture a finger, as they are very sharp. Even
after removing the bits with scissors, parts still remain and must be filed.
3. You will also note that there is no warning on Poppystamp's or any other packaging.
4. When the consumer spoke with one of the distributors, she reminded me that most of these companies
are just a mom-and-pop business. They cannot afford to have their products massproduced
{as [REDACTED] does) in China. [REDACTED is a large company that produces
dies affixed to a piece of cardboard with sticky tape. You simply remove the die from the
tape. Very safe.
5. The consumer does not want to target any one distributor. It is the manufacturer of these steel dies that
needs to be contacted, and no one will tell me who that is. The consumer suspects this is an issue of
economics, as far as the production of these dies.
6.The consumer would be content if the distributor/manufacturer could label their packaging with a
definitive warning ... one that consumers can readily see; not something in small print,
hidden in a comer on the back of the package.
justification: The consumer received a minor punctured wound on her finger, indicating an injury occurred. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible as the issue seems to be related to the design of the dye and the method of use.

incident_description: I had the Stealth - ML90451-00 in my fish tank, where it had been for months. I heard something hit the ceiling but paid no real attention to it as I was busy in a different room. A few mins later all I could smell throughout my home was burning plastic. I went into my living room to find black marks splatted all over the ceiling above the aquarium as well as the wall behind. I panicked and unplugged everything coming from the tank to find the inside part of the heater on the floor burning. Not pleased.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning aquarium heater that caused burning plastic and damage, but there was no reported injury. The likelihood of such an event is unlikely as it was an isolated incident with a specific product failure.

incident_description: My child was playing in her playpen with her Dora the explorer camera contest book. I then heard her throw up. I picked her up and she threw up quite violently 4 more times. On the last time, I realized there was a piece of plastic, almost like a laminate or a clear wrapper. I put her down and checked in the playpen to see what on earth it was and realized there was more laminate pieces laying in there. I picked them all out and then went through her toys and realized it was the dora book. It was coated in a laminate film but on the front where there is a cutout for a toy camera it wasn't secure allowing her to peel pieces of film off. I now realize the vomiting first started out with her choking and gagging which was what alerted me to pick her up. Some of the pieces were large and could have easily cut off her airway. I pealed the rest of the film off of the book and it covered both the front and the back of the book and was relatively easy to peel off.
justification: The child vomited multiple times and choked/gagged on laminate pieces from the book, indicating an injury. The likelihood is unlikely as it was a specific product failure that led to the incident.

incident_description:
We have a Oceanic Biocube 29 tank.  It has two 36 Watt Ballasts that run the lights in the tank hood.  This morning the room it was it filled up with acrid electrical smelling smoke, setting off the fire alarm.   I called 911 and the fire department responded.  I also turned off the main electrical breaker in the house.  The fire department discovered that one of the ballasts had melted and blown a hole through the case.  It also leaked potting material onto the floor.  Their opinion was that if the power had not been cut it would have quickly caused a fire in the room.

The reason I am filing this report is that when I ran a search of "Biocube and fire" on google, one of the first hits is an Amazon review that describes almost the same experience:

"4 of 5 people found the following review helpful
1.0 out of 5 stars Biocube caused fire - could have been very serious!, September 13, 2011
By [REDACTED] "formerly a Road Warrior of the Nth... (Missouri) - See all my reviews
(TOP 500 REVIEWER)    (VINE VOICE)    (REAL NAME)   
This review is from: Oceanic 82051 BioCube Aquarium, 14-Gallon (Misc.)
This review is written an hour after the local Fire Dept responded to our 9-1-1 call for smoke of initially unknown origin. Fortunately I found the source of smoke - flames erupted on the power cord from one of the transformers on the cord to our Biocube. The fire dept said we were VERY lucky to get the Biocube fire extinguished as soon as we did, the flames had already scorched the dresser AND the wall. Also thankfully the dresser is a well built structure of real wood - particle or composite board furniture would have ignited much more readily! We were just moments away from a serious tragedy. Fortunately we were home to notice first the smell then the smoke - what if we had been away???

I've often wondered at those large transformers and the very thick insulated cords. I have no idea why there is a need for such heavy duty transformers for basic lighting and a simple water pump.

I will never buy another Biocube again, from my perspective they are simply too hazardous."

It appears that this is a known issue.  I contacted the company and to their credit, they responded almost immediately, asking for pictures to send to their R&D department.  However, in light of what could have occurred, this seems like an issue that should receive some additional attention.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning ballast that melted and leaked potting material, but did not result in injury or death. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given that a similar incident was reported by another user.

incident_description:
The consumer says that on 3/2/2009 he plugged the unit in to test it out.  It was working fine.  That same day he put the incubator into his shop building and filled it with eggs and one cup of water per the instructions.  On 3/3/09 he woke up to find his shop building on fire.  The building was still standing but everything inside was completely destroyed.    

He sent the retailer and the manufacturer an email on 3/19/2009 showing them photos and a description of what happened.  He did not receive a response. He tried to save some baby goats from the fire and suffered smoke inhalation.  He required medical treatment.  He was given a respirator treatment. He also had a portable respirator treatment until he could breathe normally again. 

The consumer received a letter notifying him of the recall on August 6th 2013 (Recall number: 13-085).  His product is part of this recall.
justification: The consumer suffered smoke inhalation and required medical treatment, including respirator treatments, indicating an injury occurred. The incident was reported as a one-time event with no indication of frequent occurrences.

incident_description: My five year old son stated he felt "sick", he appeared nauseous and complained of headache and stomach ache while using newly purchased Lakeshore Rainbow Scratch paper.  He was not complaining of illness prior to using the product.  The paper smells heavily of petroleum or fuel, so much so that I became dizzy when I smelled it.  The product states it is for children 3+ and conforms to ASTM D-4236, Lakeshore Carson CA 90895, www.lakeshorelearning.com, made in China.  I am concerned about the toxicity of the product.  The product made my child ill and has no information on the packaging of what materials are used to produce the product.
justification: The child exhibited symptoms of illness (nausea, headache, stomach ache) after using the product, indicating an injury. The likelihood of this occurrence is unlikely as it is a singular reported incident with no further information on widespread similar incidents.

incident_description:
This incident occurred ahout 1 1/2  months ago,and the injury happened to my daughter. She was at her 
young son's baseball game, standing and watching;  Next to her stood her daughter, holding their cockapoo dog 
"Marley" on a leash. The leash was a "FLEXI Retractible Leash," ...the #1 brand of dog leash 
(so they claim), meant for a maximum weight pf 44lbs. M daughter's cocapoo weighs 27 lbs. I'd say it's about 1/4 inch or less in diameter and looks more like a "cable" than a leash. It was purchased at a Petco store. When another dog appeared some yards away, Marley suddenly barked and made a fast dash for him, running around and through my daughters feet first. His leash wrapped around her ankle and pulled so tightly that it imbedded itself into her flesh. It happened so fast
that there was nothing she could have done to prevent or stop it. Now, a month and a half later, the wound is as
red and visible as when it first happened. She missed days of work, had to keep her leg 
elevated, and after finally returning to her job, was sent home because of severe leg swelling.The swelling has gone down, but the scar which encircles her whole ankle will be for life. (I have pictures which  I'll attach to this email if I 
can.) Besides the statement, "Amputation/Cutting/Burning Hazard" which appears on the leash [REDACTED] there is a statement that says "Never touch leash or allow it to 
wrap around any part of body. With a playful dog attached to the end of the leash, that order is misguided and impossible. The leash should be taken off the market.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the daughter, with the leash causing a wound that has left a permanent scar, and she experienced significant disruption to her work and daily life. The likelihood of such an incident occurring is considered possible due to the nature of using a retractable leash with a playful dog.

incident_description:
"Baby's First Book", Copyright 2011, reg# PA-15501, (CN), Style# 80189 and manufactured June 2012 in Dongguan, Guang Providence, China.

Book was received in November 2012 as shower gift.  Age range listed as 0+.

Mother received book as gift at shower in November 2012, her baby was born December 17, 2012.

She gave the book to her now six month old baby for the first time to play with about June 1st, 2013.

On Thursday, June 13th, 2013 the baby had only been playing with the book for a few moments when caller heard the baby begin screaming.

She ran to the baby to see what was wrong then noticed that the baby would not open her eyes.

She examined the baby's eye which was very red around the outside, the inside of the eye was watering.

She called the pediatrician who diagnosed a scratched cornea of the right eye then prescribed antibiotic eyedrops with artificial tears.

The caller/mother has taken the book away from the baby      

Caller contacted the manufacturer Friday, June 14th, 2013 and was advised to return it to their office.

Caller plans to keep the book for CPSC first thirty days then send to manufacturer.                        

Caller sent product to mfr on 7/16/13
justification: The baby suffered an injury, specifically a scratched cornea, while playing with the book, which resulted in redness, watering, and required medical treatment. The incident was reported and the product was returned to the manufacturer.

incident_description:
We bought Sunbeam Barricade Max cat deterrent because our cats had begun spraying in the house.  This product was purchased at Petsmart.  It comes in a white bottle without any safety features to open it.  It does say keep out of reach of children on the front (but most things say that).  The back of the bottle simple says "Ready to us pump spray discourages cats from urinating, defecating, and digging in treated areas".  My husband sprayed it all over the problem area.  Immediately we noticed it was very irritating to our lungs and opened the window.  We then red the warnings and first aid.  Here it is directly from the bottle:
"if inhaled: Move person to fresh air. If person is not breathing call 911 or an ambulance.  Then give artificial respiration- perferably mouth to mouth if possible."

My husband and I had a cough for over a week after using this product.  

It the product is so toxic that it needs to explain how to give mouth to mouth resuscitation it would see that the warnings should be more evident and that there should be a safety device to prevent kids from getting into it.  The packaging is very unassuming- a cute little kitty on the front of an average looking white spray bottle.  

The active ingredients are as listed:
methyl nonyl ketone 1.9%
related compounds 0.1%
justification: The product caused respiratory issues, including a cough lasting over a week for two people, indicating an injury. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it was a singular event with specific product use.

incident_description: On the sidewalk My neighbor was walking a small dog was on the Flexi Stardard retractable leash. The dog ran around my legs and the leash cut deeply into my legs.  The first section of the leash had a flatter, wider nylon section (like a shoe lace) material. Then transitioned to a fine cord of white and black "twine" like section.  That second section as it retracted and wound around my legs and instantly cut deeply.  This could be very unsafe if it happened to a small child.
justification: The incident resulted in deep cuts to the person's legs, indicating an injury occurred. The likelihood of this specific incident happening is unlikely, as it requires a specific set of circumstances.

Aquarium Heater 120v x 60hzwith purchased from pet shop, date unknown.

Caller states that she never received notice of recall

March 27th, 2013 the heater exploded/split causing shorted circuit in aquarium, burn of power strip and ignited the rug. There was smoke and flames. Consumers feel if they had not been home, the house could have burned down.

Rug has burn approximately 12 inches by 6 inches.

Caller has not contacted the manufacturer but does intend to call them

There have been no injuries  

Close Window

incident_description: In June or July, I purchased a SEYDEL Blues G Harmonica at our local Quinn"s Music Store. It's also identified as C.A. SEYDEL SOHNE on the name plate. Sound is generated by the vibration of small reeds as you blow or draw depending on the note you want. The reason for this memo is that on one of the draw notes the metal reed dislodged and got caught on my tongue nearly being ingested. I don't know if I'd swallowed it what could have happened. None of our harmonica group have ever had this problem with any other brand of harp. I don't know if this might be a quality control problem or just an isolated incident, but I thought you should be aware of this.
justification: The incident involved a dislodged reed that could have been ingested, but no injury occurred. The likelihood of this specific event happening again is considered rare based on the user's experience and that of their harmonica group.

incident_description: Crayola bathtub fingerpaint caused a severe allergic reaction to my two year old son's hands. The skin on his hands was peeling off and bleeding after five days of use of this product. I purchased crayola bathtub fingerpaint at Stop & Shop in the baby/kid aisle and never expected it to cause harm to my child. Crayola was always a brand I trusted until now. I would never recommend this product to anyone and I plan to contact Crayola to pull it off the shelves. I have spent $1,000's medically and my child had hand pain and irritation for over 4 weeks. incident_description: We have a 3-gallon Eclipse acquarium. One night, it started to smell like something was burning. incident_description:
I recently learned that "Big Rex and Friends" cloth book was recalled in January 2010. I own that book as well as the other three books in that "series": "Fluffy Chick and Friends", "Fuzzy Bee and Friends" and "Squishy Turtle and Friends."

In light of the recall of "Big Rex and Friends," I began to look online to see if any of the other three books had been tested for toxicity and/or recalled. Disturbingly, I discovered that <healthystuff.org> had tested "Squishy Turtle and Friends" and had found high levels of toxic substances. However, I could not find any information anywhere indicating that the book had been recalled.

Here is the report:
<http://www.healthystuff.org/product.details.php?bcmode=search&getrecno=1103>

Based on this report, I believe that "Squishy Turtle and Friends" should be recalled.

Furthermore, in light of the documented toxicity of "Big Rex and Friends" and "Squishy Turtle and Friends," the other two books in this series, "Fluffy Chick and Friends" and "Fuzzy Bee and Friends,"  should be rigorously tested to determine whether they contain any toxic materials.
justification: The incident involves a product recall and potential toxicity, but no injury has been reported. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given the toxicity found in two books of the series.

incident_description:
I was changing the water in my 75 gallon aquarium.

I pulled the filter cartridge from my filter and the electric shock staggered me.  Thinking it was the filter, I unplugged it and attempted to remove the cartridge.  I was again staggered from the shock.  Since the heater was the only other electric appliance in contact with the water I unplugged it and no more electric shock.  I plugged the filter back in and no more shock.

A GOOGLE search revealed a product recall.
justification: The incident involved an electric shock that caused the person to stumble, but no injury was reported. The shock was likely due to a faulty product, as revealed by a product recall.

incident_description:
The easel as assembled per instructions has a child hazard, two dangerous "pinch points".

A child could lift the tray which widens the gap between the easel (white board and chalkboard) and the tray itself.  This allows a child to put a hand in the gap such that when the tray resumes its normal position, the child's hand is "pinched".
justification: The incident description indicates a potential for injury due to pinch points, suggesting a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is classified as 3 (possible) given that a child could intentionally or unintentionally create the hazardous situation.

incident_description:
I am an art professor in an art school.  My department originally bought 25 metal easels made by the Klopfenstein Art Equipment Co.  Almost immediately 2 of the easels fell in my classroom with no one nearby. My chairperson asked me look into it and I contacted the art store that sold us the easels. While there, I was shown another model that was almost perfectly identical, but differed in one important detail.
To explain, the original easel's angle is adjusted by a long metal rod sliding inside a metal tube. A short piece of rod is designed to turn into the tube from the side and apply pressure against the rod, securing the angle. The problem is that the long rod is very loose inside the tube and the short piece of rod is difficult to tighten.( it is all metal, without say, a rubber tip on its end) These easels weigh about 35 pounds and I believe that the locking system becomes loose from the vibrations in dragging the easels to different spots in the class.
    The other similar easel I saw uses a long square rod sliding inside a rectangular tube that fits it snugly. This  one difference makes it far safer. It also is cheaper by $75. To compound the situation, my department ignored my report and ordered 25 more of the original easels.
   The sliding metal device which secures the top of paintings uses the same system and also slides straight down and  will injure your hands if they are in the way.  Since this time, students have been injured by the sliding "tops" and perhaps by the whole falling easels. I don't know since teachers don't bother reporting the accidents.   But about a month ago, an easel fell and crashed into the head of a student sitting on  the floor. Exactly  one week later, in the same classroom, another student was beaned by a falling  easel. Both of them escaped with no injuries...this time. I seem to be the only person concerned about this. And I couldn't find any negative reports about the easels online.
justification: Injuries have occurred and the design flaw poses a high risk of future injuries from falling easels or moving parts. The fact that two students were hit by falling easels within a short period indicates a high likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description: Marineland Stealth 250w aquarium heater. I found my fish floating today and my heater was the cause my aquarium temp was over 200 degees and i unplugged the heater to let it cool off. I then plugged heat back in, out of water and it got very hot and was steaming. The heater was suppose to shut off auto out of water but did not. I lost afew good fish breeding fish at that. I would like some type of replacement. I have 3 other heaters in my other tanks aswell. what can I do from this point?
justification: The incident resulted in the death of fish, which corresponds to a severity level of 3 (Injury, but in this context, death of animals under care). The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it was a specific product failure.

incident_description: The Marineland Stealth aquarium heater, model ETP200, overheated the water in my fish tank and all the fish died. Luckily no fire or glass breakage.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of fish, but no human injury or death occurred, hence a severity level of 2. The likelihood of this specific incident is unlikely as it requires a malfunction of a specific product.

incident_description:
this is my sister in laws description:

On Thurdsday the 16th on my way back from my business trip,  I bought in the the Hudson store located in JFK airport several gifts for my nephews and my self.

incident_description: Electric Fence Controller, Model K-9, American Farmworks, began pulsing various voltages.  I disconnected unit and searched web for possible fixes.  Found a Product Recall Notice 97-031 which listed a phone number to contact the supplier.  A call resulted in a representative claiming that the company had no notice of the unit being recalled and that the company, not a governmental agency would issue the recall.  Since the unit had exceeded the warranty period, they had no further responsibility for the unit.  I forwarded the notice to the representative.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning electric fence controller, but no injury occurred. The likelihood of occurrence appears to be rare, as it was an isolated incident with a specific product model.

incident_description: Own Marineland Stealth 100.  Noticed heater had stopped working and decided to remove it when I changed aquarium water.  As I was changing the water the level dropped below the heater.  Just after I removed my hand from the water there was a bright flash and loud electrical pop from the heater.  Brown smoke then rose from the heater. I believe the flash and pop was from the heater shorting out.  Luckily I was not touching anything wet and did not have my hand in the water or else I believe I would have been electrocuted. I believe the heater has an auto stop feature when the water level is below the minimum.  I did not see the recall until I visited a pet store.
justification: The incident involved an electrical short and smoke from a malfunctioning heater, but no injury occurred. The risk of electrocution was present but not realized.

incident_description:
This  carrier has a FATAL design flaw. The first time I used this carrier was 7/4/12, Independence Day. As the fireworks started, my 11 pound docile cat popped the top and escaped into the closet. My first thought was that I had not closed the top lid correctly. WRONG! The next day, while on route to the vet, my cat popped the top open in the car. I quickly pulled over and scooted him back in and taped the lid shut. Once in the clinic's parking lot, the main hinges came open while I was holding the carrier by the handles and my cat ESCAPED into the main street! Luckily, I was able to run though traffic and grab him. This is a major safety concern.

After writing a review of this life and death safety concern, I found many other reviews of the same product that described the exact same flaw.
justification: The incident involved a pet escaping, but no injury was reported. The flaw in the carrier design led to multiple instances of escape, indicating a significant risk.

incident_description:
Richell Wood Freestanding Pet Gate, Large, Autumn Matte Finish by Richell

Got this new wooden expandable doggie gate and two days later husband forgot it was there, tripped over it, and crashed to the floor. The wood  splintered  into two very sharp dagger like pieces. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely as it required a specific circumstance of forgetting the gate's presence.

incident_description: My 2 year old daughter was playing on the floor with her books.
