incident_description:
Recently purchased an "Animal Planet" 16 foot retractable dog leash (which stated it had an 80lb capacity). 

On May 30, 2012, I took my 50lb dog, [REDACTED], outside (in my backyard) to "go potty." Prior to opening my patio door, I put the leash in the "locked" position. I opened the door and my dog did his business. Afterward, he attempted to run to a neighbor and ducks.

When [REDACTED] (my dog) ran toward the ducks, the lock mechanism (on the retractable leash) failed and my dog ran past my neighbor, which resulted in the leash rubbing and injuring the back of her (my neighbor [REDACTED]) leg. This incident would not have occurred had the lock mechanism stayed in the "locked" position.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury to the neighbor's leg, thus severity level 3. The lock mechanism failure was a singular event, making occurrence likelihood unlikely, or level 2.

incident_description:
Six days after I purchased this aquarium and set it up according to the instructions in the box, the glass fractured spontaneously (nobody injured the glass, it happened on its own; and there had been no visible prior damage, and no injury to the tank in our care).  I was sitting six feet away, and I watched as the fracture ruptured, forcing out a 6" tall by 12" wide section of the front wall of the aquarium.  The aquarium pump then forced water and glass (as well as fish) out of the tank at a long, two-foot arc.

I was injured as I cleaned up the mess.  I have a cut that was about 1.5" deep at my wrist, requiring two internal stitches, six external stitches, and antibiotics for deep tissue exposure to aquarium bacteria; I have lifelong nerve damage in that hand.  I was grateful that my children weren't home, however, since we all typically sat in the line of fire of the tank:  with the force of the water being expulsed, my 3-year old daughter would have been in danger; and we all would have been at risk for the many smaller shards of glass that left with the first large sheet.
justification: The incident resulted in injury to the person, with a cut requiring stitches and antibiotics, and lifelong nerve damage. The spontaneous fracture of the aquarium glass was an unexpected event, indicating a rare occurrence.

incident_description: I was called by my wife at work telling me that she could smell an electrical fire but could not see any smoke. She then called the fire dept who came out. There was no fire but a breaker had been flipped by my aquarium, and that is were the smell was coming from. We left the aquarium unplugged until I came home from work. I found that the electrical wire that attaches to my stealth marine-land aquarium heater had detached from the heaters base resulting in a live exposed wire in my aquariums water. I lost 4 smaller fish that were electrocuted in the incident. I have called the company and left them a message about the incident, as well as sending them an email 2 weeks ago but have not received a call back or response. I have since learned that there was a recall on the product in 2011.
justification: The incident resulted in the electrocution and loss of 4 fish, indicating an injury to living organisms, and there was no reported human injury or death. The likelihood of such an occurrence is unlikely as it involved a specific product malfunction and recall.

incident_description: The transformer for the hood on my aquarium got extremely hot and started to burn a hole into the stand where it was lying. It was too hot to touch or pick up without getting burned. I am extremely lucky that this did not cause a fire.
justification: The incident involved property damage but no injury occurred. The risk of injury was present due to the high temperature, but the likelihood seems low given it did not cause a fire or physical harm.

incident_description:
My 10 year old reef tank aquarium suffered a total loss of all life stock in a 3 hr period last Tuesday, sometimes between Noon and 5pm.
Water quality checked fine and due to the sudden onset electric is suspected.
Pumps and filters checked out fine but the moment the cord to the submerged heater was moved, the power strip suffered a catastrophic failure.
Upon inspection the Steatlth ETP150 water heater showed signs of overheating, blisters in the outer casing, some of which cracked and an almost completely burned through power cord.
justification: The incident resulted in a total loss of aquarium life, but no injury or death occurred. The failure was linked to a faulty power strip and a malfunctioning water heater.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a 5-gallon aquarium made by Cambridge Aquatics, which I understand was a brand of PetEdge. The entire line of tanks appears to have been discontinued, although they are still being sold. 

We had two goldfish in the aquarium. About a week after adding them, one ÃÂ who, granted, was sick ÃÂ got caught behind the tubing on the air pump. We got him loose, but he died within an hour. The next day, I discovered the tank leaking water all over the end table. In order to control the damage and save the surviving fish, I filled a fishbowl with some water from the tank, moved the fish into it, and drained the tank.

I bought a new tank (not by Cambridge Aquatics) the next day and, following the manufacturer's instructions, conditioned the water and let the filter run for two days before very gradually acclimating and adding the fish. But he died a couple of days later. I believe he had the same illness as his tankmate, but had the leak not forced an emergency move, he probably could have recovered.

I did let the retailer know what happened, and he offered to replace the defective tank. I appreciated that, but had already bought a new tank and would never buy anything made by Cambridge Aquatics again. I contacted PetEdge, and they claimed that Cambridge Aquatics was not their brand. Information I found at trademarkia.com says that PetEdge did indeed register the trademark Cambridge Aquatics. The packaging and instructions say the aquarium comes with a two-year limited warranty.
justification: Two goldfish died as a result of the aquarium's failure and leak, which forced an emergency move. The likelihood of this specific occurrence seems unlikely as it involved a specific product failure and a chain of events leading to the fish's death.

incident_description: On April 29, 2012, I own an aquarium heater from Marineland which stay on continously raising the temperature of my aquarium from a normal 79F to 115F. Not only did this kill almost 90% of all my Corals and inhabitants, but the heater would not shut down and continuously making a sizzling noise. Had I not caught this any early, it would probably cause more damage and could result in a fire..
justification: The incident resulted in significant harm to aquarium inhabitants and had the potential for further damage or a fire, but there is no mention of human injury. The failure of the heater indicates a product malfunction.

incident_description:

incident_description:
We received an art easel as a gift in 12/2010.  After a couple of uses and about 6 months later, I noticed the easel was unstable and screw was coming out.  As time slipped by, it became apparent that something was wrong and the easel falls down with the slightest touch from writing on the chalkboard or whiteboard.

It was finally on my list to contact the company.  I was told that I waited too long, the item is no longer under warranty.  I was informed that if I had contacted them in the beginning, they would have sent a repair kit to me, free of charge.  

My question is, if there is a known repair kit, is the company aware that something is wrong with this product?  It really is a hazard.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction (easel falling down) but did not result in any injury. The likelihood of such an occurrence is considered possible given the described instability and user interaction.

incident_description:
My wife and I purchased a book "Little Hands Love" from Piggy Toes Press from Target for our newborn daughter in either March or April of 2011.

I have just read a report from USPIRG that indicated this book has over the legal limit of lead in it.  

I would like to know what steps I should take to mitigate any hazard to our daughter and also what steps can be taken to see that these books are no longer sold.
justification: The book has been found to have over the legal limit of lead, posing a potential hazard, but no injury has been reported. The likelihood of occurrence is rare since the incident was discovered through a report and not through a direct experience of harm.

incident_description: I have been using a Marineland aquarium heater (Model: Stealth Pro 100 watt) for my 29-gallon aquarium at home since 2011. Last night (4/10/2012) it exploded by itself under normal conditions.  The heater broke into several pieces and the force of its explosion broke the back of the glass aquarium.  When I noticed it in the next morning, the back of the aquarium was almost gone.  Only a few pieces of glass remained at the corners.  Water has gone out and poured onto the wood floor of my living room.  Almost all my fishes have also gone out with the water and died on the floor.  Only three fishes were found alive at the bottom of the aquarium.  Shatters of glasses and aquarium sand were everywhere on the floor.  Water has soaked about 50% of the wood floor and a large portion of two rugs in my living room.  Some water also went into my basement through one of the house heater outlets.  While I was cleaning up the mess, I saw cupping and flaking of the wood floor at many places.  I will file a warranty claim to the manufacture and will never use their product again.
justification: The incident resulted in significant property damage but no reported injuries. The failure of the aquarium heater under normal conditions was an unexpected event.

incident_description:
When assembled, this collapsible cat cage, marketed as a "Cat Playpen," has large gaps at the corners where the panels that form the top and the sides of the cage meet. There is a 1-inch gap between the top panel and the side panels and a v-shaped gap between the side panels that is approximately 1/4 inch wide at the top, tapering down over the course of abut 4.5 inches until the two panels meet.  The flimsy construction of the cage makes it easy for an animal or a small child to accidentally catch a finger, toe, hand, or paw in this gap.
While my cat was climbing around the cage, her toe slipped into this gap and became wedged in the v-shaped space between the two side panels, and she was left dangling by her one toe.  By the time we freed her, her toe was so severely damaged that it had to be amputated, resulting in veterinary bills of over $1200.  This cage is not safe for use with animals (its intended purpose.) Small children could also easily get their fingers caught in this cage and suffer similar injury.
I am attaching photos that display the gaps at the corners of the cage. I have also used a stuffed animal to illustrate how a child or animal can get a finger, toe, hand or paw stuck in these gaps. To show how the cage should have been constructed, I have also attached a photo of a similar collapsible cage made by a different manufacturer that does not have these dangerous gaps between its panels when assembled. I have attached a photo of the cat's injured toe to demonstrate the severity of the injury.  
I also am in possession of an email sent in March 2012 by a Mid-West Homes for Pets customer service representative stating that the cage is not safe for kittens, but the product's literature and web site (see attached) describe it as a product for cats and kittens.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe injury to the cat's toe, which required amputation, and similar injuries could occur to small children. The design of the cage allows for gaps that can trap fingers, toes, hands, or paws.

incident_description:
On March 30, 2012 I went on a camping trip.  I fed my fish in my 55-gallon aquarium and noticed the water was at 78 degrees as normal per the digital temperature reader.

On April 1, 2012, I returned home from my trip to find all the fish in my 55-gallon aquarium were dead.  I checked the digital temperature reader and noticed the water was 104 degrees.

After cleaning out all of the dead fish (upwards of 35), I performed a significant cleaning and water change.  I decided to plug the Marineland Stealth Pro heater back in.  Within 12 hours, the temperature jumped from 72 degrees to 94 degrees.  I immediately unplugged the heater.

While researching the heater I discovered the recall.  I registered the product after I purchased the product from Amazon on 9/29/2010.  However, I never received any notice of an issue or recall with the heater.
justification: The incident involved the death of multiple fish, which corresponds to an incident with no injury, hence a severity level of 2. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely because the malfunction was tied to a specific product recall that not all users may experience.

incident_description: I don't think there has been an injury, although I will have my children tested for lead exposure.  In the most recent PIRG report, I found that the book "Little Hands Love" by Piggy Toes Press, has more than twice the allowable 300 ppm lead levels (I think those levels have been dropped). I have been reading this book to my children for the last year to two years. Although PIRG shows the book in its report, this book is STILL AVAILABLE for purchase on many websites, including the manufacturer's website.  This should not be allowed.
justification: The book has been read to children for 1-2 years and contains high lead levels, but no injury has been confirmed yet. The possibility of lead exposure exists due to the book's high lead content.

incident_description:
heater split in the middle.
fish tank became energized with 110 volts.
I added three fish to the tank which died.
when removing them I put my hand in the water.
I got a really good jolt with 110 volts
good thing i had shoes on and wasn't standing in a puddle
justification: The person received a shock from 110 volts while removing fish from the tank, indicating an injury occurred. The likelihood of this specific sequence of events is unlikely.

incident_description:
The heater was placed in 55 gallon tank, 2 years ago. She noticed that the fish began swimming erratically. The temperature the heater was placed on was 78 degrees but the temperature in the tank went up to 92 degrees with the heater set at 78.  A seperate thermometer is kept in the aquarium.

She touched the side of the tank and it was hot to the touch. She noticed that twenty two of the fish had died. She unplugged the heter to allow it to cool off before removing the fish. She removed the heater from the tank and throws it out in the garbage. It was then replaced with another model from the same firm. 

She contacted the retailer and they advised her that they were aware of other consumers experiencing the same failure with the tank. A few days later she noticed there was a recall online (Release #11-202). The heater I which she was currently using was also affected by the recall. The firm is going to send out the repair kit but she has also disconintued using the heater.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of 22 fish, and the retailer was aware of other consumers experiencing the same failure, indicating a possible risk. The heater was recalled due to this issue.

incident_description: The Marineland Steath ETP150 heater was used for my 30 gallon saltwater aquarium. It was set at 75F degrees and instructions were followed at keeping the water above the minimum water line and not submersing the heater at the same time. One morning, I have noticed the temperature in the aquarium had exceeded 90F and everything in the fish tank, including fishes and corals, were dead. The water was a lot warmer than usual and I immediately disconnected the heater. The heater was actually hot to the touch and I have never used the heater since. I still have the heater because I packed it away and never had the time to throw it out. Damage is approximately $400-$500 worth of fishes and corals.
justification: The incident resulted in significant damage to property (fishes and corals) but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of this specific malfunction occurring again is unlikely given that the heater was not used again and was set aside.

incident_description:
We purchased 4 16 oz tubs of Speedball "Speedy Kids" Washable Fingerpaint in fall 2010 at Pearl Art in San Francisco when the store was going out of business. We didn't open the paints until today. Three tubs were sealed with a double-layer seal imprinted with the words "sealed for freshness." Those three tubs were fine. The fourth was sealed only with a thin foil seal. The paint was chunky and had a foul odor than made us nauseated quickly (both my 4-year-old daughter and me). We closed it back up and decided we would not use it at all.

I have also reported this to the manufacturer, Speedball Arts.
justification: The incident involved a product that was not sealed properly, causing it to have a foul odor and make people nauseated, but no actual injury occurred. The likelihood of this occurrence is rare as it was an isolated incident with a product that was mostly sealed correctly.

incident_description: On December 2nd 2011 at around 4am I was alerted by the smoke alarms going off in my home as we slept. When. I got out of bed and opened the door I found a wall of smoke that immediately rushed into the bedroom. Not seeing any flames upstairs I rushed downstairs to find the top of my 46 gallon aquarium engulfed in flames to the ceiling and smoke so thick you couldn't see more than a foot. I immediately started trying to extinguish the flame with a wet towel and removing the flaming cover from the aquarium and throwing out the back door just a couple feet away burning my entire right palm in the process. I managed to get all of the flames extinguished, made sure everyone and all animals made it out of the home then opened all doors and windows. We then called the fire department to come ensure that everything was safe to leave the home. The fire department indicated that the fire looked to have come from the left side of the aquarium. The only electrical component on that side was the heater. There was extensive smoke damage throughout the entire house ruining almost all personal belongings. I suffered third degree blisters on my right hand for weeks after the fire. The following week I contacted Marineland/United pet group in which they opened up an insurance claim through liberty mutual commercial insurance for the incident. Liberty Mutual conducted many fire investigations as well as a forensic engineering exam, all proving without a doubt that the heater was defective and in fact the cause of the fire due to an internal malfunction. Then two months after the fire Liberty Mutual and the parent company of Marineland, Spectrum Brands Inc denied my claim stating that the heater was manufactured by an Italian manufacturer and merely sold under their name in the united states, intern claiming that they have no liability for this recalled product. I feel this was very irresponsible and in fact an illegal decision. I filed a previous complaint through the cpsc on Dec 2nd but would like to file another to shed light on the irresponsibiliy of the company on a product that they know to be faulty that turned my life upside down. Also I wish to file an online report so that I can provide pictures to my report to help others. They seem to be on top of helping customers with minimal damage or replacements but when it comes to destroying everything you own and forcing you out of your home for over two months the well being of their customers and making things right is not in their best interest at all.
justification: The severity level is 3 because the incident resulted in a burn injury to the person's right palm and third-degree blisters that lasted for weeks. The occurrence likelihood is 2 (unlikely) as there is no indication that such incidents are common with the product, and the investigation found a specific malfunction.

incident_description:
The Farm Innovators Inc. Heated Pet <at, a small heated mat for a cat or small dog to sleep on was used in my home for several weeks without incident. On 25-Feb-2012 I had noticed a strong odor of melted plastic in the room containing the product in question. Upon further investigation I noted that the Heated Pet Mat had partially melted. I immediately unplugged the mat attempted to remove it from the chair upon which it was placed only to find that it had fused (melted onto) the chair cushion.

Once the product had cooled enough to handle, I inspected the product. There appears to be no outward obvious reason why the product should have melted. The cat did not urinate on it (although I find it troubling that the product does not have a GFI plug since they should reasonably expect that an animal could possibly urinate on it, causing a short-circuit condition).
justification: The product malfunctioned and melted, but there was no injury reported. The incident was isolated and not expected.

incident_description:
I purchased the Aqueon Aquarium Water Changer (25 Feet Hose) for use with my 2 tanks, 30 and 50 gallons.  I have turtles, so there are more electric cords than with a standard aquarium setup.  For each tank, I have a heat lamp, uva/uvb lamp, submersible heater, and filter/pump, so there are 8 cords in the room.  

The adapter fits the sink fine.  It's easy and doesn't leak.  The hose connects at one end to the sink adapter and at the other end to the vacuum. It's easy to push it on and get a tight seal.  

The product worked amazingly well!  But just as the first tank was approaching the fill mark, the hose flew off the sink adapter!  It flew in a 3 foot arc, flinging a large amount of water outward in a large area at high velocity.  In 1 second, half the room was soaked - including the power strip!!  The strip was turned off, but we quickly unplugged it anyway.

In 8 subsequent attempts to reconnect the hose to the adapter, it flew off, slinging water in every direction.  This product is going to electrocute someone, or their aquatic pets - if it hasn't already.
justification: The incident involved a high-velocity water spray that soaked a power strip, which was turned off but posed a risk of electrocution, and despite no injury reported, the risk of injury or death is present. The repeated failure of the hose to stay connected under normal use conditions indicates a significant risk.

incident_description: Wiring of aquarium heater (Marineland Stealth model#ETP200W submersible aquarium heater) short-circuited where wire enters plastic casing. This caused the wiring and plastic wire insulation to melt and caused smell of electric fire in aquarium, which spread throughout the house. Wife noticed the smell and called 911 who brought fire department out. The heater has been recalled already and Marineland is sending a replacement. We wanted to notify you of the damage for your records and ongoing investigations.
justification: The incident involved a short-circuited aquarium heater that caused damage but no injury was reported. The likelihood of occurrence is considered unlikely as the issue was specific to a recalled product and prompt action was taken.

incident_description:
The product is the  Oceanic 82051 BioCube Aquarium, 14-Gallon (Misc.) - the following is the review I wrote on Amazon on Tuesday, September 13, 2011 about an hour after the O'Fallon Fire Protection District responded to my 9-1-1 call for help for smoke of initially unknown origin: 

This review is written an hour after the local Fire Dept responded to our 9-1-1 call for smoke of initially unknown origin. Fortunately I found the source of smoke - flames erupted on the power cord from one of the transformers on the cord to our Biocube. The fire dept said we were VERY lucky to get the Biocube fire extinguished as soon as we did, the flames had already scorched the dresser AND the wall. Also thankfully the dresser is a well built structure of real wood - particle or composite board furniture would have ignited much more readily! We were just moments away from a serious tragedy. Fortunately we were home to notice first the smell then the smoke - what if we had been away???

I've often wondered at those large transformers and the very thick insulated cords. I have no idea why there is a need for such heavy duty transformers for basic lighting and a simple water pump.

I will never buy another Biocube again, from my perspective they are simply too hazardous.
justification: The incident involved a fire that was extinguished before causing injury, but it had the potential for serious harm. The fire was an unlikely event, as suggested by the reviewer's surprise and the rarity of such incidents.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that while her 10 month old child was playing in her play yard she grab the book and lost her balance and fell face forward on the book which caused her to receive lacerations to cornea of her eye.  She was taken to the Serria Vista emergency hospital where she was treated and sent home.

Consumer stated that she had not contacted the manufacturer as yet.

Consumer feels that this book is a safety hazard and should be reported.
justification: The child received lacerations to the cornea of her eye, indicating an injury occurred. The incident seems to be a one-time event based on the information provided.

incident_description: I have a Marineland Stealth Aquarium heater, Model # 90450-00 which apparently broke. Was changing water in aquarium when I received an electrical shock through the water. All fish went belly-up.  I unplugged the heater and called Aquarium store where purchased. Apparently there was a recall on all these heaters, which were listed as dangerous. I went to Marineland's website and got an 800 phone number to get a replacement or refund. No one answers their phone.
justification: The incident resulted in an electrical shock to the person, which corresponds to a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood of occurrence is classified as unlikely (2) since it was related to a specific product recall.

incident_description:
Safety concern:  I purchased a children's activity book from a gift store in Westerly, R.I. 
I asked for gift wrapping and was intending to give it as a Christmas gift for an 8 year old boy.
In re-wrapping the gift prior to Christmas I noticed a "Caution" statement on the back of the book which reads :
 "CAUTION: drawing stylus has a functional sharp point. Keep particles of scratch coating away from eyes, as irritation may occur.  In case of accidental contact, flush eyes with water.  Avoid inhaling particles of scratch coating. Use in a well ventilated area under close adult supervision. Not for children under 5 years of age."
1. this product contains potentially [REDACTED]/harmful substances and should not be marketed/especially for children.
2. Had I not seen the Caution statement, I may well have given this potentially dangerous book to an 8 year old child who could well have used it unsupervised and/or shared it with other children in the same manner.
3.  This book should be recalled immediately and the publisher notified that they are producing/promoting a potential health hazard for children, or anyone using this product!
Book title:   An Art Activity Book/ Solar System Scratch and Sketch  for inquisitive artists and astronauts of all ages.
ISBN 978-1-59359-917-1
2006 Peter Pauper Press, Inc/202 Mamaroneck Ave, White Plains, NY 10601
justification: The incident involved a potentially hazardous product being purchased for a child, but no injury occurred as the caution statement was noticed. The product's hazards and potential for misuse suggest a moderate likelihood of occurrence.

incident_description:
The consumer stated that he has a recalled aquarium water that was cited in release 11-202 and it  malfunctioned killing the fish in his tank. The consumer found that the tank was at 100 degrees. The consumer stated that he noticed the heater was in fact hot. The consumer has not experienced any property damage. The consumer did not call the fire department after the incident took place. 

The consumer stated that the heater was hot to the touch and burned his right hand in his palms in minor fashion. The consumer did not go see a doctor. The consumer has been unable to reach any one at the firm when he called the firmÃÂs recall hotline. 

The consumer stated that the water heater does not appear to show signs of damage. The consumer has not called the retailer. The consumer stated that his fish tank did remain intact. The consumer owns 3 of the recalled aquarium heaters.
justification: The consumer suffered a minor burn on their right hand, indicating an injury. The incident involved a malfunctioning product that caused harm, but the injury was minor and did not require medical attention.

incident_description: I have a Marineland Stealth ETP250-250W aquarium heater that malfunctioned.  The cord came loose from the heater and killed all the fish in my marine tank.  We noticed an electrical burning smell after this happened and I traced it back to the heater.  I researched the heater and found that Marineland recalled the heater.  I have been a firefighter for 30 years and realize that I am extremely lucky that this did not cause a more serious fire incident in my home!  Substandard products like this kill people and burn down houses!  Fortunately for me, I only lost a few hundred dollars worth of livestock.
justification: The incident resulted in the loss of fish but no human injury or death occurred. The malfunction was discovered after the fact, indicating it was an unlikely event.

incident_description: The Marineland Stealth Heater in our 24 gallon Nano Cube malfunctioned & killed our Mandarin fish, our mated pair of Redi Seahorses, and our feather duster.  When we came home from work, the temperature in the tank was over 100 degrees.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of multiple aquatic animals, and the malfunction of the heater led to a significant increase in water temperature. The likelihood of this specific malfunction occurring is unlikely, but not impossible, given the nature of equipment failure.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that he smelled an odor of electric fire and discovered that the aquarium heater was sparking and cracked open, this caused fatality to his fishes and corals.  He was not aware what was causing the problem, so it took him several hours to figure out that it was caused from the heater to eventually unplug it.

Consumer stated that this incident is estimated at a damage of $3,000. He had experienced similar problems of Release #11-202.

12/5/11 Consumer contacted the manufacturer and was advised to send in the report of damages which included all documentation and proof to this incident.
justification: The incident involved an aquarium heater malfunctioning, causing damage to the consumer's fishes, corals, and property ($3,000), but no human injury or death occurred. The consumer had experienced similar problems before, suggesting some level of recurring issue.

incident_description:
I have a safety concern about "Spy Net Night Vision Infrared Stealth Binoculars" manufactured by JAKKS Pacific model # 18738

My wife and I were checking on our sleeping son before we went to bed.  He had fallen asleep with the toy's lanyard around his neck. Although the lanyard has a breakaway link, it had twisted around itself ahead of the link rendering it useless. It took considerable effort to untwist the lanyard. I cringe when I think of the morning we could have awaken to had we not discovered this incident. I hope by reporting this, I can save a parent from a terrible tragedy.  I have removed the lanyard from this toy as I believe it is dangerous and unnecessary. I recommend the manufacture put out a recall notice immediately to take the same action.
justification: The incident involved a potential choking hazard with a toy's lanyard, but fortunately, no injury occurred due to parental intervention. The likelihood of this specific occurrence is considered possible given the design of the product and common child behavior.

incident_description:
Signature Fundraising is a company that provides fundraising services to schools.  A prize for turning in a certain amount of orders is an Air Guitar.  You can see it on page three of this link

http://www.signaturefundraising.com/Signature_Website_2011/site_resources/prizeoverload_brochure/Default.html

This toy uses a laser pointer on the bottom of the unit.  There is no warning on the box about this laser.  I contacted Signature Fundraising and they replied stating they have contacted the manufacturer and were told the unit does not use a laser but is like a TV remote.  You can see a video of this toy in action here.

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-3hbe_B5G-Q&feature=related

You can see the laser shining on the persons hand as he is strumming the instrument.  Signature Fundraising says this toy is safe but I have never seen a  TV remote shoot a laser out of it.  From what I understand these lasers can cause temporary blindness.
justification: The toy's laser pointer could potentially cause temporary blindness, but there is no reported injury. The likelihood of occurrence seems possible given the presence of a laser without warning.

incident_description:
On my Oceanic 14 gallon biocube aquarium top, I removed the hood to replace both lights in it.  I unplugged the unit from the outlet to replace the lights.  After replacing the lights in the hood, I connected the ballasts connectors to the electrical cord unit (unit is still unplugged from wall at this time).  I then connected the electrical plug into the wall outlet.  No lights came on.  I turned the light on the hood and that is when the ballast caught fire with a blue fire about 1" shooting out of one of the ballasts.

My husband unplugged the unit from the power.  I then removed the hood canopy.  There are fire burns to our stereo speaker system that was next to the ballast when it was on fire.  Additionally, on the ballast connector, there is a hole  from the fire that was shooting out of it.  Picture is included in this report.

My husband was watching the entire incident and can confirm what happened.
justification: The incident involved a ballast catching fire, causing damage to nearby equipment, but no injury or death occurred. The fire was extinguished by unplugging the unit, indicating prompt action prevented further harm.

incident_description: On November 20th, I purchased the Tetra Waterfall Globe 1.8 Gallon Kit at Petco, for my 7-year old son. My wife was cleaning the bowl for set-up and barely nicked the edge of the sink. The glass cracked and splintered into pieces. I was shocked to see that the thickness of the glass was less than a potato chip! My wife sustained a small cut, but it could have easily been worse. I can't believe that we paid over $60.00 for this hazardous merchandise! I have purchased many other fishbowls from various stores before that were at least 5x the thickness! I'm sure that glass is not that expensive and they could offer a safer product. Acrylic would be a better option since many of these units would be purchased for small children. This product is a danger to anyone that has purchased it. I was not about to return the pieces of glass to the store, but expected a response.  I contacted Tetra's website first and they claimed that they would respond within 24 hours. They did not bother to repond at all! Petco has offered a replacement, but I believe this to be unacceptable due to its unsafe characteristics.
justification: The incident resulted in a small cut to the wife's hand, classifying it as an injury (severity level 3). The likelihood of such an incident occurring is unlikely (occurrence likelihood 2) as it involved a singular product failure.

incident_description: I have 9 turtle aquariums that have all been using the Stealth Pro underwater heathers for approximately 1 year or just a little less. About 2 months ago, one of my 75 gallon tanks way overheated during the night. The turtle that lives in that tank is an approximately 7ÃÂ water turtle. The water temperature in all my turtleÃÂs tanks was normal when I turned off their lights for the night. (I check everything in all the tanks both morning & night to make sure all is OK.)The next morning when I turned on his lights he jumped off his basking platform into the water immediately began swimming back & forth frantically. Luckily I saw him do that & went to get him out to see what was wrong. During the night his water felt like it had heated to almost boiling. Luckily he spent the night out of the water on his basking platform. I was shocked when I put my hand in to get him. It scared me to think how long he was actually in that extremely high water temperature.
justification: The turtle was exposed to extremely high water temperature, likely causing stress, and was fortunate to have escaped the water to avoid more severe consequences. The incident indicates a potential for harm but no explicit injury details are provided.

incident_description: Fire started at Aquarium. Aquarium heater shorted out caught fire.
justification: The incident involved a fire due to a shorted-out heater, but there is no mention of injury or death. The likelihood is unlikely as it is not a common occurrence for an aquarium heater to short out.

incident_description:
The product from GSI, is called GSI QUALITY ULTRA-SAFE ELECTRONIC 50W INDOOR PET HEATING COMFORT MAT ÃÂ PASHM MATERIAL ÃÂ ROUGH 24ÃÂ INCHES the UPC code on this product  is SD1sBBb0jR. The bed lit fire while in use, resulting in 1880.32 in damages to my home as well as killing my dog, Rawr. Thank you for your time.

incident_description:
I just learned about this product recalled and requested a refund from the manufacturer.  I then finished reading the recall notice and found the request at the bottom that asked incident reports.

The Marineland Steath Aquarium heaters thermostat failed and raised my marine aquariums temperature to 95* before the failure was detected.  Many delicate corals in the tank were killed.  The heater was being used as directed, and when the thermostat failed the heater continued to heat the tank water to lethal levels.
justification: The incident involved a product failure that caused damage to property (corals in the aquarium) but did not result in injury or death. The likelihood of such an occurrence is unlikely as it was an isolated incident with a specific product failure.

incident_description:
Marineland Stealth Aquarium Heater: ETP150-150 watts:  I have had the heater for a couple of years. The heater has always been set at 75 degrees F, and never moved.  Last week I noticed that my corals were all limp.  I checked the tank temp and it was at 86 degrees F.  I unplugged the heater, let it cool down and removed it. I iced the tank to slowly bring down the temp.  I replaced it with another Marieland Stealth EPT-250-250 watts which I have as a back up (I have three Marineland Stealth heaters in all).  Today, while at my local fish store I wanted to by another one and was told that there had been a recall and that I should check out Marinelands website. He told me that I should remove all three heaters.  I did.
The Marienland site had your link (disabled!), so I did a search and found that you would still like input.
Now that I have read that there may be over 1 million of them out there, I am bothered that the retail distributers were not bound to post this recall/"warning" on their front door where all their customers could see it.  
Thank you.   [redacted]
justification: The incident involved an overheating heater that was addressed before causing injury, but it had the potential to cause harm to aquatic life. The user's proactive measures prevented injury, but the situation posed a risk.

incident_description: The product is a toy book with soft covers and an open plastic ring. The plastic ring is used to attach the book to another device, such as a book bag or a play gym. In this case, within an hour of using the toy for the first time, the ring snapped apart into three pieces. I took pictures - the ring is made up of three parts, two of which are small enough for a child to choke on.
justification: The incident involved a product failure with potential choking hazard, but no injury occurred. The likelihood is unlikely as it happened within the first use for one customer.

incident_description: My nine-month-old baby was playing with a removable piece of a children's book called Thank You, Lord (illustrator Leslie Ann Clark, published by Christian Art Kids 2009). The book, which is made of colorful foam covered with paper, includes several removable foam pieces, kind of like simple puzzle pieces. Without me noticing, he chewed a plastic film off the foam piece and put it all the way into his mouth and closed his mouth. I noticed that he appeared to be chewing something and pulled it out of his mouth. The plastic/cellophane piece is about two inches across and hexoganal. It is printed with an illustration. It is a very sturdy material and could certainly cause choking/suffocation. It is not evident when looking at the book that it is covered with a film. Finding it in my baby's mouth was a frightening experience. The book is labeled for "ages newborn and up." It says, "Non-toxic" and "This is not a teething toy," but babies chew on books, and this book is clearly not suitable for babies. (And the non-toxic label seems to acknowledge that children might chew it.) I feel it should have a choking hazard warning and the icon that indicates that a product is not suitable for children under three. The content of the book is fine for all ages, but the plastic/cellophane film on this book is very dangerous and, as my baby demonstrated, readily chewed off by a baby.
justification: The incident involved a baby putting a potentially hazardous material into their mouth, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of this occurrence seems possible given that babies often chew on objects, including books.

incident_description: I checked the temperature on my saltwater aquarium as I do every morning, and the temperature had spiked to over 95 degrees, I unplugged and removed the heater from the tank, but it was too late, my corals and my oyster died. : (
justification: The incident resulted in the death of corals and an oyster, but no human injury occurred, thus it's an incident with no injury. The likelihood of such a spike happening again is unlikely given that corrective action was taken.

incident_description: I recently purchased a Hyper Pet Duck sling shot toy from Cabela's.  After carefully reading the instructions on the package, I went outside to play with the toy with one of my Golden Retrievers.  Upon the third time of pulling back the toy, the slingshot apparatus inside completely broke.  The metal piece inside sliced open my hand, forcing me to have 4 stitches put in at the base of my thumb.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical attention (4 stitches), and the failure of the toy's component was unexpected but not necessarily rare given variability in product durability and usage.

incident_description:
I had a Marineland Stealth Pro heater for my 20 gal tank.  I noticed it had started hissing one day and soon after, I noticed a bump on the heater rod.  Soon after that, it looked like something was leaking from that same area so I took it out of my tank.  It looks like it got too hot and blistered and its innards were leaking out.  I have since lost 3 neon Tetras and a Glowlight Tetra for seemingly no reason (my water parameters were fine).

I called Marineland but never got an answer.  I emailed them but never got an email back.  Very disappointed with the company.

I just found out about this recall (9/18/11) so unfortunately I had replaced the Stealth Pro with a Stealth.  The Stealth stopped working a couple of days ago -- not exploded, just not heating anymore.  I woke up to find my tank at 72 degrees when it's normally 85!
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning heater that caused a leak and resulted in the loss of fish, but did not cause any human injury. The likelihood of such an incident happening again is possible given the history of issues with the product.

incident_description:
Caller stated that her aquarium heater blew up on Monday. The consumer's neighbors heard a loud explosion. The consumer found glass gravel and dead fish. Her floor also flooded as a result. The consumer is not sure if there is any structural damage to her home but there is water damage. The consumer stated that no one was injured. The consumer had an 80 gallon aquarium. The water was set to 84 degrees. The heater was 250 watts. The product has been  recalled as part of release 11-202. 

The consumer called the firm about this yesterday and they offered to replace the heater, the cost of the fish tank and the damage to her home. The consumer called the retailer yesterday and they agreed to send her the receipt of purchase for the heater via email. The water heater blew up in small pieces and emitted a smell of burning plastic.
justification: The incident involved property damage and a product malfunction but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of such an event is unlikely given that the product was recalled.

incident_description:
I purchased a Cat Tree Condo Scratcher Bed 40-inch from Overstock.com, the manufacturer of the item is Go Pet Club, model # GPC-F21

Within 24 hours of assembling the product, (5) 9-week-old kittens destroyed the material that made up the bottom "tent" portion of the tree, by simply climbing and playing on it.
The material became mere threads of string, where one of the kittens got entagled aroud the neck and could not get out. I had to cut the frayed string of the material with scissors to get him free. Had I not walked in when I did, it is quite possible that kitten would have been strangled to death.    

Overstock was helpful, they let me return the product for a refund.  I wrote a negative review of the product on the Overstock sight.  
I also tried to contact GoPet Club via their "contact us" tab on their website, twice. I have revceived no response to my written complaint/concern regarding the safety of this product. This prodcut poses a danger to crawling toddlers and small children, in additon to pets, as the furniture is at floor level and easily rips, tears, and becomes a stringy mess in a very short amount of time.
I did take photos showing proof of the defective (cheap) material.
justification: A kitten got entangled and could have died if not freed in time, indicating a potential for severe injury or death. The product's material failure led to an incident with injury.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that the circular rim of the helping magnifier he purchased is very sharp. The consumer has bought 3 of these products from the retailer. The consumer's daughter cut her right index finger when she tried to remove the protective plastic from the magnifier, resulting in a her applying a band aid. She did not go to the doctor nor seek medical attention. The product is a manual tool. The incident occurred as soon he presented product to his daughter and she tried to open the product. The consumer has yet to call the retailer about the product but does intend to return two of the magnifiers. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer about this incident. 

Update:  Consumer returned all 3 back to the recently opened Braintree store on Aug 09, 2011 (store #351)  (Copy of return receipt enclosed)
justification: The consumer's daughter cut her finger while trying to remove the protective plastic, resulting in a minor injury that did not require medical attention. The incident was isolated, as it was a one-time accident with a product that the consumer has bought multiple times.

incident_description: Amazing Baby Feel and Learn soft toy book has a [REDACTED] string attached with 2 plastic rings.  This is a baby item for infants.  6 month old daughter was playing with this and got the string completely wrapped around her neck.  Luckily she was being supervised and we were able to get it off of her and she did not get strangled.  This could potentially have been a very serious situation.  This item is sold on the internet and sold by the company amazing baby.  They should not sell baby toys that have strings attached as this could pose a strangulation risk.  It is sold at many retailers as well.
justification: The incident involved a 6-month-old child getting a string wrapped around her neck, but she did not suffer an injury due to supervision. The item's design poses a strangulation risk, making it a potential hazard.

incident_description: After placing the collar on my cat, there was a large amount of loose powder. My husband was nuzzling with the cat and playing and subsequently inhaled the substqance. He immediately became dizzy, disoriented, lost feeling in his limbs, eyes dialated, and became almost giddy. I immediately took him outside and washed his nostrils with saline. After being outside for approximately 30 minutes he felt better. During this time, I went back in and removed the collar and cleaned up the powder residue from the cat. I opened the windows and turned on the air to try to remove any airborn powder left. When he returned inside the dizziness returned but not severe, nor did the other symptoms reoccur. He did experience a throbbing headache when all was done. I realize the allergic reaction he had was probably rare and due to the inhalation of the product immediately after being put on, but if this had been a child, I fear the damage could have been more severe or permanent. There is a warning to wash hands, but nothing regarding children, inhalation, or ingestion of the product. After receiving the MSDS sheet, the primary inert ingredient is acetic acid ethenyl ester, polymer with ethene which is used in anesthetics and alcohol.
justification: The husband experienced symptoms of dizziness, disorientation, and loss of limb feeling after inhaling the powder, indicating an injury. The symptoms were temporary and alleviated with treatment, but could have been more severe if the exposed person was a child.

incident_description: My grandson was in his bed reading a "Baby's first"book by Hinkler Books Pty. Ltd. When I went to check on him a few minutes later, he had torn the cover off the book and was playing with stuffing or padding the manufacturer had placed underneath the book cover. It was white in color and he was tearing it apart and could have easily ingested the material. The book lists as it's e-mail hinklerbook.com and has an Austrailian address.
justification: The incident involved a child ingesting potentially harmful material, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of such an incident happening is possible given the design of the book.

incident_description: THE BUCKLE PORTION OF A M2PETS HIP HUGGER LEASH SUDDENLY AND UNEXPECTEDLY DISENGAGED DURING USE AND FLEW BACK AND STRUCK CLIENT IN THE EYE. EYE HAS BEEN SEVERELY INJURED AND THE INJURIES ARE PERMANENT.
justification: The incident resulted in severe and permanent eye injuries, classifying it as an injury. The unexpected disengagement of the leash buckle was an uncommon event.

incident_description:
we had a marineland stealth pro heater in our 90 gallon aquarium, that exploded today, Aug.7 2011
the heater shattered, killing most of the fish, and sending burnt glass all over the aquarium and water out of the top of the tank.  everything in the tank was damaged, and it has taken over 12 hours to try to empty the tank.  everything needs replacement.  we needed to purchase a temporary tank and supplies, and will need to completely re do the original tank, fuses were blown in the home. we are only lucky our home did not catch fire.  the tank is destroyed, fish are dead, our carpets are soaked, and needless to say, we are very upset.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of most of the fish and damage to property, but there is no mention of human injury or death. The likelihood of such an event occurring is unlikely, as it was described as an unexpected failure of a product.

incident_description:
Regarding a PetsMart Black-Finish Wrought Iron Aquarium Stand.

I found my 18 month old toddler child with her neck caught in the narrowing portion of the leg of this aquarium stand. She was gasping for air and could not cry. She could not pull herself back out of it either. Fortunately I am attentive and noticed it quickly. She certainly would have suffocated within a minute.
  
This stand was bought locally at PetsMart in Denton, TX. I found the following online:
http://reviews.petsmart.com/4830/2754149/black-mountain-forge-black-finish-wrought-iron-aquarium-stands-reviews/reviews.htm
justification: The child suffered a near-suffocation incident with physical distress, but no lasting injury reported. The likelihood is unlikely as it required specific circumstances and prompt intervention.

incident_description: I purchased a MARINELAND STEALTH PRO 200 WATT AQUARIUM HEATER and several months later recieved a recall on it (i had noticed it making a popping sound and not keeping correct temperatures) so i disconnected it and purchased a [REDACTED].
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction (popping sound, incorrect temperatures) that did not result in injury, but prompted a recall and replacement. The likelihood is unlikely as the issue was specific to the product and not widespread.

incident_description: After about one year my super expensive, "high quality", "fail safe" Stealth Pro 300w aquarium heater just turned on in the middle of the night and did not turn off. By the time I went to feed my $500 special breeder fish the next morning the water was 120F and I had very expensive fish soup!
justification: The incident resulted in a significant loss of expensive fish, but there was no injury or death reported. The likelihood of this specific failure of a 'fail-safe' device is unlikely, but not impossible, given the context.

incident_description: The consumer says the product overheated her fishtank.  The consumer says the heater was so hot her husband burned his hand.  The consumer says her husband unplugged it and took it out of the tank.  The conusmer says the unit was not supposed to have been running because the temperature was fine.  The consumer contacted the manufacturer who will replace the unit.  The consumer said all the fish died.  The unit is recalled under Release # 11-202
justification: The consumer's husband burned his hand, indicating an injury occurred. The incident was specific and not part of normal operation, suggesting it is unlikely.

incident_description:
IÃÂm writing about the Novel Dog Trailer from Dutch Dog Design aka DoggyRide.com (http://www.doggyride.com/us/en/P2/Novel-Dog-Bike-Trailer.aspx).  The tow bar is designed so that it is about 3 inches off the ground when attached to the bike.  When turning left the tow bar can and does hit the ground causing the trailer to want to bounce to the right (NewtonÃÂs Law Third Law of Motion).  Depending on the speed of travel and extent of turn the bounce of the trailer can and will cause the bicycle to flip to the right causing a crash.  

I encountered this problem on Saturday July 2, 2011 resulting in a crash while turning left on a right hand banked curve.  During the crash the bicycle was flipped more then 90 degrees to the right resulting in me sliding down the road on my right side, all the while hearing the trailer sliding behind me making me think that it was going slam into me from behind.  It did not; in fact it stayed coupled to the bike.  Sometime during the few seconds it took for all of to happen my left thigh made impact with the bicycle. The crash was followed by a trip to the local Emergency Room with multiple injures to myself including a possible muscle separation in my left thigh.  I required a CT with contrast to make sure that my femoral artery was not leaking.

My dog was also injured with many minor cuts and contusions as she was ejected through the front opening even though she was attached to the leash set included with the trailer.  The leash set was adjusted to its shortest possible length.  My dog weights about70 pounds, which is 30 pounds less, then the limit of the pet capacity for the trailer.  Since my dog was attached to the trailer and ejected and then stopped by her neck she could have been severely injured or killed.

The crash also damaged my bicycle; the total extent of damage is still to be determined.  It does have a bent rear wheel, which will have to be replaced and broken off components on the handle bar.  Furthermore it is very possible that the frame is bent.  The bike was flipped more then 90 degrees to the left.  If the frame is bent then the bicycle is no longer safe to use and will have to be totaled.

My wife emailed the manufacture on July 5, 2011 with the following;  ÃÂWe purchased a doggie ride trailer so that we might take our dog touring with us this fall.  During one of our rides, my husband was making a left hand turn and the tow bar bounced on the pavement and caused the trailer to flip over on its side with my dog flying out through the head hole even though she was buckled in.  Major damage to the fabric on the trailer.  We also question the integrity of the frame and tow bar of the trailer as it flipped so easily to the right side.   The trailer then flipped my husbands bike over to the right resulting in major injury to him and his bicycle.

Is this a common problem with the doggie ride trailer?  How do we go about getting repairs to the trailer?  Of course, I do not even know if I can get my dog to go near the trailer again.

[REDACTED]ÃÂ

Their response on the same day was; ÃÂ[REDACTED],

I am very sorry to hear about your accident. I hope your dog and husband are recovering well. This is not common and many people tour for long periods of time with the DoggyRide without incident. I have copied the owner/designer on this email so that he address your concerns and about the integrity of the frame and assist in ordering replacement parts. 

Again, I am truly sorry about this incident and we will be in touch soon. The owner is out of the office for a couple days and he will get back to you at his soonest availability. 

Warm Regards,
-- 
dutch dog design | customer service | 425.292.9257ÃÂ

I am now recuperating at home.

I have been making the above mention turn for the better part of twenty (21) years with and without a bicycle trailer (different brand) attached to my bike without incident.
justification: The incident resulted in multiple injuries to the rider, including a possible muscle separation in the left thigh, and minor cuts and contusions to the dog, justifying a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 2 (unlikely) because the manufacturer stated that this is not a common problem and many people tour with the DoggyRide without incident.

incident_description:
Cat's Pride litter [purchased at Stater Bros.] clogs not only the cats nose, causes sneezing and watery eyes it does the same to humans.  Consumer says the product made her sick.  When adding it to the litter box it was so dusty that she had to cover her face, hold her breath and run from the room before inhaling.  She got a sick feeling from the dust and fragrance.  It wasn't fragrant,  it was a nauseating smell, the dust it produces is ridiculous, the worst she has experienced- bad enough for her to file this report.  

All symptoms stopped when the litter was removed.
justification: The consumer reported getting a sick feeling, sneezing, watery eyes, and a nauseating smell from the dust and fragrance of the litter, indicating an injury. The symptoms stopped when the litter was removed, confirming the product caused the adverse reaction.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to report that her daughter suffered 3rd degree burns when her Life of the Party soap making kit malfunctioned. The consumer stated the instructions off the product were very vague. On the outside of the product it states that it is marketed for children 12 and older with adult supervision, where as the instructions on the inside of the box don't mention anything about adult supervision and stated the product is for ages 9 and up. The consumer's daughter, as directed placed the solid wax from the product in 1 and 1 half inch chunks into a measuring cup then placed it into the microwave. The product indicates to place the wax in the microwave for 40 seconds at 10 second intervals. Her daughter removed the product from the microwave, then placed a few drops of color and proceeded to stir the product. Afterwards, her daughter placed  the product in the plastic mold intended for shaping the wax.  

Right after stirring the contents, the mold container exploded and hot wax projected itself on to the consumerÃÂs daughter face. The product went from her right eye resulting in 1st degree burns and up to her forehead just below her hairline resulting in 2nd degree burns. The consumer had her attorney contact the manufacturer. The consumerÃÂs attorney sent her a letter on May 24th, 2011 stating that he has been in contact with an officer from Life of the Party. The consumer stated that her attorney will also call the retailer. The consumerÃÂs daughter was taken to the Provina St. Joe's Hospital in Joliet,IL after the incident for a couple hours and a cold compress placed on her head, while the hospital were in contact with another hospital for the duration of her stay. The consumer by direction of the hospital in Joliet, then had to take her daughter to Loyola hospital in Maywood, IL 40 minutes away from the hospital in Joliet. 

Her daughter was in the hospital overnight until five o'clock in the afternoon the next day. Her daughter was given Tylenol with codeine as well as bassatracin ointment. The consumer had to take her daughter to the hospital in Loyola 3 days after the incident for a follow-up examination. Her daughter was not referred to a primary care physician but has to have an SPF of over 100 for the summer to avoid sunburn on the affected area. The consumer has been directed by her attorney to file this report to the CPSC and express just how unsafe the product is.
justification: The consumer's daughter suffered 3rd degree burns, specifically 1st and 2nd degree burns on her face and forehead, indicating a significant injury. The incident was caused by the product malfunctioning, suggesting that while not inevitable, such an occurrence is possible.

incident_description: My Marineland Stealth Pro Aquarium Heater exploded shattering my 30 gallon tank, sending glass 5 feet across the room, and causing extensive water damage to the carpet and structure below. In addition we lost numerous fish and had to throw out the filter which was broken in the process.
justification: The incident involved property damage and loss of aquarium contents, but no injury was reported. The severity is classified as 2 (Incident, No Injury) due to the absence of reported injuries.

This killed 2ea Brilliant Blue Diamond and 1ea Mandarin Orange Discus, 6ea Skunk Cory and 3ea Siamese Algae Eaters. The concussion broke a glass cover and airstone. incident_description: Returned home from a 4 day vacation to an overwhelming smell that something had burnt (burning/chemical smell).  Upon searching, I found that the Stealth Pro fish tank heater (model ML90453 - 250watt) in my 90 gallon tank had apparently exploded and several of my very expensive cichlids were dead.  There was debris all over the tank (black plastic and black unknown substance).  I was VERY FORTUNATE that the tank didn't break or the explosion didn't result in a fire.   I'm not sure exactly when this occurred but from the look of my dead fish, it happened within a day or two prior to my returning home.

Reading the reports maybe we were lucky the tank didn't burst or start a fire.  It could have been worse but pretty horrifying, overall - especially for our fish and traumatic for our kids

incident_description: Had a Marineland Stealth  ETP150 Heater in my 75 gallon tank and my fish were large angel fish that I had for over two years. They all died at once and I couldn't figure it out until I put my hand in the water, it was over 100 degrees Fahrenheit .

incident_description: This report concerns the Marineland Stealth Pro aquarium water heater.  At about 2am, the product apparently exploded while in the tank.  I heard a noise and went to investigate, but didn't realize the source of the noise until morning when checking on the fish.  Fortunately, nobody was injured (except for many of our fish).  I am now aware the this product has a voluntary recall, but wanted to ensure that your were aware of continuing issues with the product.  I am just thankful that there were no serious consequences, but the potential certainly exists.  I'm not sure if this forum permits pictures, but I did take one prior to returning it to the pet store as the visual display is pretty impressive at the violence that it must have exerted.
justification: The incident involved an explosion, but fortunately, nobody was injured. The product has a voluntary recall, suggesting potential ongoing issues.

incident_description: I have several fishtanks in my home. I have always used Marineland Stealth heaters.  unfortunately, they always seemed to stop working within one year of purchase; therefore, I have had to purchase several replacements throughout the years.  Frustrated, at the quality of most products these days (nothing seems to last), I simply repurchased the same brand as I felt safer with the plastic sheath around the glass heater and just figured the products weren't meant to last, but at least my fish would not be able to break the plastic sheath.  A few months ago, I noticed a load cracking sound coming from 2 of my tanks.  Sounded a bit like gravel hitting the glass but much louder.  I thought the fish were moving gravel and hitting it against the glass.  Not the case.  Turns out the heaters were malfunctioning and almost bursting through the plastic sheaths that protect the heaters.  I unplugged the malfunctioning heaters, removed them and noticed large bulges along the plastic sheaths.  Very hot to the touch.  I called the company, but the hold time was too long to wait.  Happened again a few weeks ago.  I replaced the heaters with new backup heaters (same type and brand) that I always keep on hand.  I tend to buy multiples at  a time in case of an emergency. For several months my fish had been acting wierd. They would get excited at the same time and hit the tank sides, as if they were startled. This would happen at different hours of the day/night. Maybe they were getting electrical shocks from the malfunctioning heaters!!!
justification: The heaters malfunctioned and posed a risk to the fish, but there was no reported injury or death to humans or fish. The likelihood of occurrence is considered possible given the repeated malfunctions of the same brand and model of heater.

incident_description:
I had a marineland Stealth aquarium heater, I believe it was a ETP 150.  In January ago I noticed that the top had "popped off".  I was concerned about electrocution, so I unplugged the unit.  When I removed it from the tank, there was a strong smell of burning plastic coming from the unit.

Since then I have replaced that unit with another, I will now be contacting the manufacturer for a replacement.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning aquarium heater with a strong smell of burning plastic, but no injury occurred. The low likelihood is based on the fact that it was a single incident with no widespread issues reported.

incident_description: I purchased a Marineland Stealth 250W aquarium heater about 18 months ago and installed it in my 55 gallon aquarium.  Approximately two months ago I came home to find that a putrid burning electronics smell was coming from my aquarium.  I unplugged the aquarium and drained half the water from it.  When I removed the heater it was too hot to hold in my hand and there was smoke rising from the top.  It took three water changes over the next three days to bring the temperature of my water down to the right level.  All but one of my fish survived.  Just happy that I came home when I did and that there was no further damage.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning aquarium heater that caused a burning smell, smoke, and required multiple water changes, but did not result in injury or death to humans or fish (except one). The severity is classified as 2 (Incident, No Injury) due to the potential for harm but no actual injury.

incident_description: bought a brand new stealth heater for my fish tank and everything was going great, came home from work and all my fish were dead.......my thermometor said my tank was 105o I lost $75.00 worth of fish and I never used that heater again......I thought Stealth was suppose to be a good brand, guess I was wrong
justification: The incident resulted in loss of property (fish) but no injury or death occurred. The likelihood of such an incident happening again is unlikely as it was a one-time failure of a product.

incident_description: I bought OUT! Moisture Lock training pads for my dog.  The pads are folded in the package.  I went to place a pad down for my dog and shook it in the same manner you would shake a sheet or pillowcase to unfold it.  When I shook it, the end burst open (or was not sealed properly in the first place) and I was sprayed in the eyes with the product inside (little pellets).  The pellets stuck to my eyes and it began to burn and I was not able to see clearly.  I began to flush my eyes while my husband consulted the package for information regarding ingestion or contact with eyes and the package said nothing.  I called the question/comment line listed on the package.  The incident happened before their normal business hours and their message told me to call CHEMTREC in case of a medical emergency.  I called the number on the message and the man who answered said that they were not medical professionals and to call poison control.  The woman at poison control was able to tell me that the product contained ammonia and alcohol and that eye irrigation was needed.  After sufficiently irrigating my eyes, my eyes were fine although they burned for several hours and I developed a headache.  My concern is the absence of warning information on the package about ingestion or contact with eyes.  The only warning on the package was a suffocation warning about the plastic packaging.  I was also concerned about the company I was told to call in case of a medical emergency that was not able to help me.
justification: The incident resulted in injury, as the person suffered eye irritation and a headache after being sprayed with product. The likelihood of occurrence is unlikely, as there is no indication that this is a common issue with the product.

incident_description: Regarding small book made by Fisher Price called "Numbers with Teacher Terry".   The recommended age group for the book is 1 to 4 years old, however it is definately a choking hazard for my 1 year old son. The book is made out of cardboard, and after only playing with it for a few minutes he had several large pieces of the cardboard pages in his mouth.  Most one year olds still put everything in their mouths as they are teething.  A book meant for this age group should be more durable.
justification: The incident involved a 1-year-old child putting large pieces of cardboard from the book into their mouth, indicating a potential choking hazard, but no injury was reported. Given the age group and teething behavior, similar incidents are likely to occur.

incident_description: The Imaginarium Deluxe Easel Starter Kit contains plastic cups for painting.  After the first use, I was washing the cup and cut my finger very badly on the jagged plastic that was sticking up from the bottom of the cup.  It would've required stitches but the cut was so jagged/mangled that it wasn't possible.  Upon inspection of the other cups in the kit, the rest also had jagged plastic on the insides, although not to the extent of the one that cut my finger.
justification: The incident resulted in a severe cut that required medical attention but not stitches due to its jagged nature. The presence of similar jagged edges on other cups in the kit suggests a potential for repeated injuries.

incident_description: K & H OUTDOOR HEATED KITTY PAD MODEL NUMBER 3093. WE USED IT INDOORS ONLY FOR ALMOST TWO YEARS AND YESTERDAY NOTICED IT WAS OVERHEATING SIGNIFICANTLY AND ACTUALLY MELTING THE PLASTIC CASE. NO ONE WAS HURT AND LUCKILY THE CAT DID NOT HAVE ACCESS TO IT OVER THE WEEKEND OR IT WOULD HAVE BURNED HER SEVERELY. NORMALLY HEAT IS EXTREMELY MINIMAL SO AS NOT TO BURN AN ANIMAL.
justification: The incident involved a product malfunction causing overheating and damage, but no injury occurred. The likelihood of this specific malfunction is considered unlikely as it was not a typical operating issue and the product had been used safely for almost two years.

incident_description: A two-year old child died as a result of ingesting a coin-sized battery. The battery was from a pet tracking tag which attaches to the dogs collar called Paw Scout.  The dog had chewed on the collar and battery housing and the battery had fallen on the floor unobserved.  Medical care was provided on several occasions over the next few days. Unfortunately, the girl's symptoms mimicked her brother who had the flu. The girl died as a result of ingesting the battery on September 26, 2021.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a two-year-old child. The likelihood of occurrence appears rare as it involved a series of unlikely events.
